The win moves United level with Liverpool in the WSL, with both teams three points off the European places.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola spotted for first time since seismic guilty verdict against Man City: Club's former boss attends Paris Fashion Week alongside his daughter after breaking silence
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola has been spotted enjoying Paris Fashion Week, marking the first time the former Manchester City manager has been seen in public since the bombshell verdict.

It has been a turbulent week for the decorated Spanish football manager. First, there was the seismic announcement of Manchester City's guilty verdict for financial rule-breaking over a nine-year period, two years of which Guardiola was in charge.

Then the Negreira scandal reared up again in Spain, with 50,000 pages of evidence compiled by Real Madrid landing at UEFA on Thursday, accusing arch-rivals Barcelona of making illicit payments to an influential referees' chief. The allegations also cover a four-year period during which Guardiola was in charge of the Catalan side.

For Guardiola, who departed City in the summer saying he needed to rest and 'take a step back', the past few weeks have been anything but peaceful, with his glittering legacy coming under scrutiny like never before.

Victoria Beckham's fashion show certainly appeared to provide some welcome relief, then. Guardiola enjoyed the evening at the Conciergerie, located at 2 Boulevard du Palais, once a medieval royal palace and French Revolution prison, alongside his daughter Valentina on Friday night.

He looked effortlessly stylish as he leaned against a lamppost in the French capital, wearing a striped black shirt and dark trousers as he entertained frequent requests for photographs.

Guardiola enjoyed the evening at the Conciergerie, located at 2 Boulevard du Palais, once a medieval royal palace and French Revolution prison, alongside his daughter Valentina

It marked the first time Guardiola has been spotted in public since City's bombshell verdict

After leaving City in the summer, Guardiola said of his plans for the future: 'Rest. No plans to train for a while. Otherwise I would be here. I need to step back, I will not train for a while,' he said. 'Many people when I said it will be my last season said after three months you will come back. I don’t think so, I will take a while, but I have to prove to myself (that I need a rest).'

Whether he feels differently now that demands are being made for two of his three clubs to be stripped of the glittering array of titles he won remains to be seen.

In the case of City, there has been no suggestion that Guardiola was complicit in any of the financial doping.

He firmly planted his flag with his former employers earlier this week, writing on social media: 'I want every single Man City fan to know I am here; more than ever.

‘I am, always have been, always will be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran (Soriano, CEO), the players, staff, Enzo (Maresca, manager) and you, our unique supporters.

‘Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all.’

The club were accused by the top flight of ‘sham’ deals during the period they became the major force in English football.

In a damning 40-page verdict, City artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules.

The eight-times champions were found guilty of ‘all charges related to serious breaches’ of the regulations and the majority of those in relation to its failure to co-operate with the competition’s probe.

City witnesses were also accused of lying in front of the three-person panel, in an explosive verdict that sent further shockwaves through football after news of the guilty verdicts first emerged on Friday.

During press conferences across his tenure, Guardiola always said he ‘trusted’ those in charge of the club and said he would front up to them if and when they were proven

During press conferences across his tenure, Guardiola always said he ‘trusted’ those in charge of the club when quizzed on the charges and said he would front up to them if and when they were proven.

As for Barcelona, they have repeatedly denied any wrongdoing against allegations that they paid more than £7million in a series of payments over 17 years from 2001 to Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira when he was vice president of Spain's technical committee of referees.

Guardiola was head coach of Barca for four seasons in the heart of this era, from 2008 to 2012, during which he created a team generally accepted to be among the best to ever play the game.

The club claim the money was paid for scouting and technical reports provided by a company belonging to 81-year-old Negreira since the story broke in 2023.

At the time, Barcelona president Joan Laporta said: 'Let it be clear Barca have never bought referees and Barca never had the intention of buying referees, absolutely never.'

LaLiga claimed they were unable to investigate because of the time elapsed since the alleged offences were so far in the past.

UEFA did launch an investigation although it appeared to be going cold until the matter resurfaced this year as Florentino Perez ran for re-election as president of Real Madrid with promises to get to the bottom of what he called 'the biggest scandal in history'.

On Thursday, UEFA issued a statement to confirm a 'substantial amount of documents' had landed at the door of its ethics and disciplinary inspectors and will be assessed.

Sports.title: Something on your mind, Mateo? Man City star Kovacic misses OPEN GOAL in Croatia's clash with England
Sports.content:
Manchester City midfielder Mateo Kovacic sensationally missed an open goal while playing for Croatia against England – with fans wondering whether club issues were playing on his mind.

Kovacic, 32, has played for City since 2023, but now finds the club engulfed in a war with the Premier League that has seen them found guilty of the vast majority of their financial charges.

City are appealing the verdict, but it emerged on Friday night that one of their main defences surrounding sponsorship from Etihad could be in tatters due to the brand previously stating they are state-owned.

And those issues could have played into Kovacic's international form as he missed a golden opportunity on Saturday.

The midfielder found himself around eight yards from goal with a pretty much empty net to pass into, but sliced wide.

He had won the ball off club team-mate Elliot Anderson, rounded Jordan Pickford, and only had to roll the ball into the net – but failed.

A STUNNING miss from Mateo Kovačić 🫣



The Man City man rounds the keeper and misses an open goal. pic.twitter.com/YfPuDehwYf — ITV Football (@itvfootball) October 3, 2026

Manchster City midfielder Mateo Kovacic missed a sitter while playing for Croatia against England on Saturday

'Kovacic missed an empty net after all that work,' one fan wrote on X. 'These City players look traumatised by the 114 charges.'

Another posted: 'These City cheats are literally quivering in their boots whilst playing knowing what they all are.'

England manager Thomas Tuchel had previously admitted the Three Lions' City players are nervous about their futures.

While City stress their innocence and have appealed the decision, Tuchel admitted that Marc Guehi, Elliot Anderson and Nico O'Reilly are naturally anxious.

The trio have been inundated with calls and messages over the past week, with O'Reilly now having flown back to Manchester for treatment on an injury.

'Are they worried or are they concerned? I think that would be a very human reaction if you don't know what's going on for the club that you signed,' Tuchel said.

'They're still young. They're ambitious. They're told they are totally innocent and don't know what's going on.

'We speak about it at dinner and at a table of eight or 12 people. Of course, we speak about it at breakfast.'

Kovacic's club face a potentially significant punishment after being found guilty of financial breaches against the Premier League

Tuchel claimed that the news around City being found guilty of the vast majority of charges had represented a 'distraction' before then clarifying that the City trio had been focused in meetings and training sessions.

'It's a big topic in camp,' he added. 'We had some time off between the matches and it is a big subject. How can it not be a topic? We talk with them but only briefly.'

The German did also suggest that he would continue considering picking players in the event that they are relegated from the Premier League as a punishment, should an appeal fail.

'I would always try to pick the best team for the camp, occasion, tournament,' he said. 'I will never rule that out because they don't play in the top flight in their country. We need to look at it case by case.'

Sports.title: Why Alex Scott can rival Declan Rice and the moment that showed Man City star's mind may have been elsewhere as England strike perfect balance in 7-0 Croatia thrashing, writes JACK GAUGHAN
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel was back to being serenaded by the band of travelling support once Anthony Gordon had put the Nations League tie to bed with England’s third before half time.

Argentina might not be forgotten but the 100 fortunate enough to make this trip to western Croatia were imploring their manager to give them a wave.

He didn’t, they playfully jeered and England continued pouring on the pain for an embarrassed Slaven Bilic.

The most complete performance of Tuchel’s reign answered some post-World Cup questions and provided a blueprint moving forward as they attempt to evolve, writes Daily Mail Sport's JACK GAUGHAN from Rujevica Stadium.

A perfect cocktail

Tuchel has talked over the past few days of using that second half against Croatia in Dallas as a ‘memory’ to build on. When England, in his words, were ‘free’ and ‘took the risks that were worth taking’ during the group stage victory.

That is not necessarily just releasing the shackles without thought but picking their moments and there was enough of that for England to truly mix things up. Goals deriving from counter attack positions and goals from more patient build-up, Jude Bellingham’s a product of a 27-pass move.

That particular passage of play suddenly quickened and devastated an ageing Croatia, just as Harry Kane’s did minutes after the break, coming from a slow approach involving Alex Scott and then Elliot Anderson breaking lines.

It was a blend of English qualities: players capable of mastering the ball but players who happily lean into their physicality as well.

Tuchel talked over the past few days of using that second half against Croatia in Dallas during the World Cup as a ‘memory’ to build on

Jude Bellingham’s goal against Croatia, England's second, was a product of a 27-pass move

Dovetailing

Clearly Tuchel wants more genuine competition for places and aside from the goalkeeping situation has even referenced Declan Rice as somebody who might be mindful of those coming up behind him in midfield.

One is Bournemouth’s Scott, paired with Anderson in behind Bellingham. The 23-year-old’s performances in training across camp have caught the eye and his cameo in Prague did too.

'His first start and what a start,' Tuchel said here at full time. 'He is so smooth on the ball, his decision making. He plays with so much confidence. He is so active. The work rate off the ball makes him the complete package. We had a lot of variety in the centre of the pitch.'

The way in which Anderson and Scott were so at ease with each other – be it mopping up or instinctively knowing who goes and who stays – was built in the Under 21s last year, when lifting the European Championship trophy.

They are close, immediately gelling off the pitch and part of a coffee club during that tournament in Slovenia. Incidentally, one of the first occasions Scott met Tuchel was the night England won that competition, the England boss accidentally tapping his broken jaw during celebrations in the dressing room.

If that might have been painful, Scott’s presence in Rijeka saw Anderson look as comfortable as he ever has in an England shirt, albeit against wounded opposition.

Minds elsewhere?

Anderson appeared serene for the vast majority of it, running midfield, although there was one mistake that had seemingly allowed Manchester City team-mate Mateo Kovacic to nick one back for the hosts.

Anderson dallied in his own box, his pocket picked, but Kovacic inexplicably smashed wide when presented with effectively an open goal from eight yards. The 6,000 schoolkids collectively gasped.

These sort of incidents have been commonplace for City stars over the international break, which is understandable given the bombshell verdict of financial impropriety at the club and the uncertainty around that.

The way in which Anderson and Scott were so at ease with each other – be it mopping up or instinctively knowing who goes and who stays – was built in the Under 21s last yea

Crafty Kane

Croatia broke in a brief moment of excitement for the home crowd, Martin Baturina ahead of anybody in an England shirt. The vuvuzelas began to screech. And then, from nowhere, the last man came to the rescue, expertly reading the game and cutting out the counter. Kane, that was.

Kane was further back than anybody and generally this could have been the deepest he has ever operated for England.

Time and again he dropped off the front, basically operating as a No8, to engineer chances for others, most notably punching through the lines when finding Jarell Quansah in the build up to Gordon’s header.

He might be bearing down on the likes of Robert Lewandowski in the list of all-time international goalscorers but Kane continues to offer so much more for Tuchel.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury plans to invite 'old buddy' Donald Trump to be part of his ringwalk for £150m mega-fight with Anthony Joshua: 'I'll definitely make the offer!'
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury plans to invite 'old buddy' Donald Trump to be part of his ringwalk for £150m mega-fight with Anthony Joshua: 'I'll definitely make the offer!'

Tyson Fury has suggested he will try and persuade United States president Donald Trump to join him for his ringwalk when he takes on Anthony Joshua in December.

Fury met the president at the UFC Freedom 250 event at the White House in June, joining Trump, First Lady Melania Trump and a host of MAGA royalty on the South Lawn.

He raised eyebrows with a cap, which featured a particularly bold message of support for Trump. 'Donald Trump for Prime Minister', it read alongside an embroidered British flag.

The slogan was a nod to Trump's signature red 'Make America Great Again' caps, which he sported throughout his election campaigns.

It was there Fury said he was keen to take on Joshua in the near future – and that fight has come to fruition, and will take place on December 11 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

And Fury is keen to have his friend there. He said: 'I'll definitely make that offer to my old buddy, old pal, and we'll see if he's available.

'Probably unlikely because of the situation he's in at the moment, being the President of the United States.'

Tyson Fury (centre) has said he will ask Donald Trump (right) to join his ringwalk when he faces Anthony Joshua

Though Fury may want Trump in his corner, Joshua will literally have a Fury in his, with Tyson's uncle, Peter, part of Joshua's group of trainers.

Tyson shrugged off suggestions that Joshua would have the inside track claiming that he hadn't spoken to him in years, but his father John was even more emphatic in discussion with Playbook Boxing, hinting at a betrayal from his brother which meant that he will 'never speak to him as long as (he) lives'.

'If he was to do that (talk to Joshua) in any way, shape or form, that would make him the lowest form of human being,' John stressed. 'Even thinking about doing it, that makes him the biggest dog, the biggest untrustworthy dog of all time.

'If he's going to start giving phone calls and advice, meeting in secret, giving him secret sessions, he's a f***ing cockroach.

'The only advice he could have wanted is on Tyson, isn't it? There is no smoke without fire.'

As if speaking directly to Peter, he finished: 'Son, give your head a wobble. Don't sell your soul to the devil for a fiver.'

Peter shared on social media that he had spoken to AJ 'two months ago' about 'advice on his skill set', calling the Londoner 'a really nice guy'.

'After his fight anything he needs from me (would) be a pleasure. He has a great team around him (including) Team Usyk.'

Sports.title: Centurion Andy Robertson believes victory over North Macedonia can be used as a platform for Scots to hit new heights
Sports.content:
Scotland captain Andy Robertson believes the team will go from strength to strength after claiming their first win under new boss Sebastien Pocognoli.

On a night which saw skipper Robertson win his 100th cap, the Scots were utterly dominant as they beat North Macedonia 2-0 in their Nations League clash in Skopje.

Kieron Bowie set them on their way to victory with a terrific finish from outside the box after just seven minutes, the 24-year-old striker notching his first goal for his country.

The Scots missed multiple good chances and also had a penalty ruled out by a VAR check after an apparent foul on the excellent Ben Gannon-Doak.

But they still had far too much for the North Macedonians, with John McGinn stepping up to score a penalty in the second half after a handball by Rangers striker Bojan Miovski.

As was the case against Switzerland, the Scots finished the match with 10 men after a late red card to Scott McKenna, but this was a much-needed boost for Pocognoli in his third match at the helm.

Scotland captain Andy Robertson takes the acclaim of the Tartan Army at full-time in Skopje

Robertson almost capped his centurion status with a goal in the 2-0 win at North Macedonia

Delighted to get the new era up and running, Robertson said: ‘I thought we were excellent. I thought we done really well on a really difficult pitch.

‘I thought we could have been four, five-nil up at times, and then we didn’t take the chances.

‘We made it a wee bit interesting for ourselves towards the end. But then I thought we defended so well for the last 10 minutes, defended our box and kept a clean sheet.

‘So the performance all round was really good. It was a big win. You want to get it for the manager as early as possible — and thankfully we’ve done that tonight.’

Robertson became only the second player in history to reach 100 caps and now sits only two behind the record of 102 held by fellow Liverpool legend Sir Kenny Dalglish.

He looked like a man possessed at times last night, firing four good shots at goal in the first half in particular.

‘I thought I was going to get his (Dalglish’s) goalscoring record as well,’ joked the skipper about the number of shots he had. 'But I think he’s got that one safe in the bag.

‘I believe I’ve still got a lot to give for this country. Hopefully the performances are showing that, apart from the pass (leading to the red card) to Scott McKenna! I apologise for that.

‘I’ll need to go in to say sorry to him. But the guys did a really nice presentation in the afternoon for me.

‘I think my message was clear: I just wanted to win. You always want to remember these.

Skipper Andy Robertson and Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli at the full-time whistle

‘I always remember my first game as captain, we got beat 4-0 at home to Belgium. So it was a bit bittersweet.

‘But tonight, thankfully, the lads done so well to get the win. That will be memorable for a long time for me and all my family.

‘It’s been such an amazing journey. I love Scotland, I love playing for my country. It is a special achievement.’

It was a hugely encouraging night for Pocognoli, whose side dominated from the first whistle to the last in Skopje to clinch his first win at the third time of asking.

The Scots will now round off the international window when they take on Slovenia back at Hampden on Tuesday night.

‘I’m very pleased with this first win,’ said Pocognoli. ‘I think we played very well, created a lot of chances, we’ve kept two clean sheets which means a lot also.

‘It was a nice game. Not everything was perfect because we should have scored more goals.

‘Kieron Bowie scored the most difficult goal from the game. I was really pleased for him because I know the topic about not scoring will have been on the table after 25 minutes.

‘I was happy for him, it’s his first goal [for Scotland]. I was really pleased with his performance and many of the lads.’

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel says Jude Bellingham has 'gone up a level' since the World Cup as he lavishes praise on star man after England's 7-0 rout of Croatia
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel says Jude Bellingham has 'gone up a level' since the World Cup as he lavishes praise on star man after England's 7-0 rout of Croatia

Thomas Tuchel hailed Jude Bellingham after another scintillating night in an England shirt, believing that the Real Madrid superstar has gone up another level in recent months.

Bellingham scored one and recorded a hat-trick of assists during the demolition of Croatia, with team-mates queuing up to lavish praise on the vice-captain.

The 23-year-old became the first midfielder to record four goal involvements in an England match for since David Platt scored four against San Marino in 1993.

Roy Keane claimed that Bellingham 'can go on to become one of the greatest players of all time' and Tuchel has seen more improvement.

'At the moment it seems like [he has gone up a level] and you always need to,' Tuchel said. 'The level you showed last week is never enough, it's just the nature of football.

'It's like you can never stand still, it's like walking against an electric escalator. You have to develop and push for the next level. That is always necessary.'

Jude Bellingham impresses again as he continues to break records in an England shirt

Bellingham created an astonishing eight chances and laid on for Bukayo Saka's first goal seconds before half time.

'He was amazing tonight,' Saka said. 'He deserved [England] player of the year and he probably deserves man of the match tonight as well. He was special. I'm happy to play with him and happy to have him in the England team.'

Tuchel admitted that the atmosphere in a stadium populated by 6,000 schoolchildren and 100 away fans was 'strange' but couldn't hide his excitement at the way in which England dismantled Croatia.

And he believes nights like this are a way of erasing the pain of July's World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina.

'The speed and technical quality, the hunger off the ball, was the very highest level,' the German said. 'I'm very happy about the attitude. We were never arrogant, always humble. It was a complete 90-minute performance.

'If you feel pain you have to play with the pain. The same with disappointment. It was not easy at the beginning of the camp. We'll always have a scar, feel pain, but this is the way to move forward. We've played in the same manner all three matches.'

Sports.title: Larry Nassar controversy takes fresh twist as police dispute claim Team USA gymnastics doctor was removed from Michigan sex offender registry
Sports.content:
Disgraced Team USA gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar was never on Michigan's sex offender registry, it has emerged.

It was reported earlier this week that Nassar, who served as team doctor for the national gymnastics team from 1996 to 2014, had been quietly removed from the state's registry.

However, Michigan State Police have now disputed that claim, revealing that the serial sexual abuser was not on the list in the first place.

'Information suggesting that convicted sex offender Nassar was removed from the Sex Offender Registry (SOR) by the Michigan State Police (MSP) because of the Smith decision is incorrect,' Lori Dougovito, a spokeswoman for Michigan State Police, told The Daily Mail in a statement.

In Michigan, only sex offenders living in the state are required to comply with and appear on its sex offender registry.

'Offenders not currently domiciled, temporarily residing, working, incarcerated, or going to school in Michigan do not have the duty to register in Michigan under Michigan’s Sex Offender Registry Act (SORA), and would not be visible on Michigan’s public Sex Offender Registry (SOR),' Dougovito added.

Michigan State Police have disputed a report that disgraced Team USA gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar (pictured) was removed from the state's sex offender registry

Nasser is serving decades in prison after being convicted of multiple crimes

'Should the offender later domicile (including being incarcerated), temporarily reside, work, or go to school in Michigan, they would be expected to register and be placed on Michigan’s public SOR if still required under SORA at that time.'

Nassar is currently being housed at FCI Lewisburg in Pennsylvania. He has served time in federal, out-of-state prisons since pleading guilty in 2017.

Should he return to a prison in Michigan, Nassar will then be entered onto the state's sex offender registry, police confirmed.

Nassar, a former Michigan State University and USA Gymnastics doctor, used his position to exploit hundreds of young athletes, including medal-winning Olympic gymnasts Simone Biles and Aly Raisman.

He is currently serving multiple prison sentences lasting decades after being convicted on multiple counts of sexual abuse and child pornography in both federal and state court.

Nassar's federal conviction in 2017 on child pornography charges carried a 60-year sentence. Should he survive to serve the full sentence, he will then be required to serve 40 to 175 years in Michigan prisons on seven state-level sexual assault charges in Ingham County.

He also faces a 40-year to 125-year prison sentence in Eaton County on additional sexual assault charges.

Speculation that he had been removed from Michigan's sex offender registry began earlier this week following a social media announcement from the Eaton County (Michigan) Prosecutor's Office.

Nassar is pictured in court during his sentencing hearing in Michigan in January 2018

Nassar, a former Michigan State University and USA Gymnastics doctor, used his position to exploit hundreds of young athletes, including Team USA gymnasts

The post claimed that the 63-year-old Nassar was among more than 20,000 people whose names have been removed from the sex offender list after the Michigan State Police recently purged thousands of individuals from the database whose crimes happened before July 1, 2011.

A Michigan Supreme Court ruling on September 9 said that amendments to the Sex Offender Registration Act issued in 2021 cannot be used to retroactively require registration due to older incidents, leading to the purge of the database.

The prosecutor's office wrote on social media that: 'The Michigan Supreme Court's decision to eliminate SORA requirements for these offenders is deeply concerning. Our community, along with the victims of these crimes, expected the registry to provide a measure of protection and awareness - assurances that have now been removed by the Court's ruling.'

The registry is intended to 'assist the public' with preventing future criminal sexual acts by convicted sex offenders, according to Michigan State Police, and typically lists a legal name, photo, primary address, work address, age, physical description and court with records relevant to the criminal conviction.

The Eaton County Prosecutor's Office issued a statement on Friday, correcting its original post.

'We must correct our earlier social media post about removal of convicted sex offenders from the Michigan Sex Offender Registry,' it wrote. 'After reporting from the Detroit News, it appears that Larry Nassar was never actually registered under the Michigan Sex Offender Registry.

'We never contemplated that one of the most notorious sex offenders in the history of the state would not have been registered despite the law requiring otherwise. In our experience, when a sex offender is sentenced to a term of incarceration, they are listed in the Michigan Sex Offender Registry as being “incarcerated” and complaint (sic). That status does not change until the offender is released from custody, at which time the entity incarcerating the individual ensures the registry is updated.'

More than 150 gymnasts were abused by Nassar during his 30-year career. Nassar admitted to sexually assaulting the athletes when he worked at Michigan State University and USA Gymnastics.

Olympic icon Simone Biles was among Nasser's long list of hundreds of victims

The doctor also admitted to possessing child pornography, and more than 100 women sought over $1billion from the federal government for the FBI's failure to stop him.

He was sentenced in federal court in 2017 to 60 years in prison on charges of possessing child sex abuse material. The following year, Nassar was sentenced to up to 175 years and up to 125 years, respectively, in two separate Michigan courts for molesting female gymnasts under his care.

Following the federal sentencing, U.S. Attorney Birge said: 'Today was a day of reckoning for Larry Nassar. He more than deserves this punishment for what he did.

'He consumed child pornography on a massive scale. We found 37,000 images of child pornography on his computers. Insatiable hunger of that nature simply encourages those who produce such images to continue to sexually exploit children. Compounding his danger to the public,

'Nassar was an insidious hands-on child predator in his own right. He took advantage of family friendships. And he treated his license to practice medicine as a license to sexually molest children. Thanks to the brave victims who came forward, we learned the full scope of his depravity. The breadth and dark depth of his heinous acts are extraordinary.'

In April 2024, the US Justice Department announced a $138.7 million settlement with more than 100 people who accused the FBI of grossly mishandling allegations of sexual assault against Nassar in 2015 and 2016, a critical time gap that allowed the sports doctor to continue to prey on victims before his arrest.

When combined with other settlements, $1billion now has been set aside by various organizations to compensate hundreds of women who said Nassar assaulted them under the guise of treatment for sports injuries.

Simone Biles publicly broke her silence in January 2018, revealing in a powerful tweet that she was one of Nassar's victims.

'It took me a long time to write that, probably a couple of days, because every time I would go to write, I would start bawling, and I couldn't get through it,' she said.

Biles also noted that she was heartbroken over having to continue to train at the ranch, the former USA Gymnastics national training center where she and her teammates were abused by the disgraced doctor.

Sports.title: Chelsea LOSE behind-closed-doors 'training exercise' friendly to Portsmouth as Xabi Alonso focuses on tactics with his side holding the worst defensive Premier League record
Sports.content:
Chelsea LOSE behind-closed-doors 'training exercise' friendly to Portsmouth as Xabi Alonso focuses on tactics with his side holding the worst defensive Premier League record

Chelsea lost 2-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly to Championship side Portsmouth on Saturday afternoon as they prepare for the return of the Premier League.

The secret game against Pompey – revealed to be taking place by Daily Mail Sport earlier this week – involved some Blues players who are rehabbing their way back to fitness.

Chelsea face Bournemouth next in the Premier League at Stamford Bridge on Saturday October 10, after this three-week international break has ended. The Cherries are winless in the league under new head coach Marco Rose after five match rounds.

Also involved against Portsmouth were some younger players from the Chelsea academy alongside first-teamers, while sources added Xabi Alonso used it for tactical work. It was described by insiders as a training exercise, first and foremost, and so they are not alarmed by the scoreline in any way.

Senior stars have been away on international duty, such as Morgan Rogers, who scored the seventh in England’s 7-0 win over Croatia in the Nations League on Saturday.

Portsmouth, managed by John Mousinho, are 19th in the Championship and preparing to play the South Coast derby against arch rivals Southampton next.

Xabi Alonso's Chelsea lost 2-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly to Championship side Portsmouth

One major area of focus for Alonso in this break has been how to stop opponents from scoring. His team have the worst defensive record in the Premier League this season after conceding 12 goals in five games.

One decision he will need to make versus Bournemouth is whether to persist with his three at the back, or move to a more traditional system involving a back four.

Alonso has shown a fondness for secret friendlies, having set up two in the summer against Crawley and Bromley before their pre-season trip to Australia and Asia. They won those, but not against Portsmouth on Saturday.

Sports.title: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture

Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.

The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter.

Image: Ireland's players bowed their heads before facing Israel in the reverse fixture last week

Hallgrimsson later labelled the accusation a "verbal attack" during a separate briefing for members of the Irish press.

The exchange in the main press conference took place after Hallgrimsson was also asked a question about a co-pilot who attacked a pilot and tried to hijack a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.

The reporter's question was shut down by the FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there are no open UEFA investigations at this stage from the previous meeting between Israel and Ireland last weekend.

The FAI are conducting their own investigation into whether striker Adam Idah was racially abused by Israeli supporters during their 3-0 UEFA Nations League win but have yet to make an official complaint to UEFA.

Image: Protesters interrupted Ireland's draw with Austria by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch with Palestine flags on them

Despite the high-profile nature of the fixture, members of the Irish media later reported that there was no UEFA delegate present at the news conference.

Sky Sports News was told a UEFA match delegate does not have to attend press conferences. The duty is left to the venue media manager, whose job it is to report anything if there is an incident.

Sunday's match is being played in Backa Topola, Serbia, as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott.

Sky Sports News has approached the FAI for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: John Fury hits out at brother Peter, calling him a 'cockroach' for joining Anthony Joshua's camp ahead of Cardiff showdown
Sports.content:
John Fury called out his brother Peter for being a 'cockroach' after his estranged brother joined Anthony Joshua's camp ahead of the Briton's showdown with his son Tyson in December.

The long-awaited Battle of Britain is set to take place in Cardiff after months of back-and-forth between the Fury and Joshua camps, but neither John nor Peter will be in the corner of the Gypsy King, after Joshua announced this week that Fury's uncle had helped with his preparations.

Eyebrows were raised due to Peter's family ties, but Fury shrugged off suggestions that Joshua would have the inside track claiming that he hadn't spoken to him in years.

His father John was even more emphatic in discussion with Playbook Boxing, hinting at a betrayal from his brother which meant that he will 'never speak to him as long as (he) lives.'

'If he was to do that (talk to Joshua) in any way, shape or form, that would make him the lowest form of human being,' John stressed. 'Even thinking about doing it, that makes him the biggest dog, the biggest untrustworthy dog of all time.

'If he's going to start giving phone calls and advice, meeting in secret, giving him secret sessions, he's a f***ing cockroach.

John Fury called out his brother Peter (left) for potentially helping Tyson's rival Anthony Joshua ahead of their Cardiff showdown (pictured in 2015)

'The only advice he could have wanted is on Tyson, isn't it? There is no smoke without fire.'

As if speaking directly to Peter, he finished: 'Son, give your head a wobble. Don't sell your soul to the devil for a fiver.'

Peter shared on social media that he had spoken to AJ 'two months ago' about 'advice on his skill set', calling the Londoner 'a really nice guy'.

'After his fight anything he needs from me (would) be a pleasure. He has a great team around him (including) Team Usyk.'

John may have been staunchly defensive of Fury in the context of Peter doing anything to sabotage him in the ring, but relations between father and son remain minimal after having been, in John's words, 'completely destroyed'.

The duo are at loggerheads over Fury Junior's career, with his father adamant that he should prioritise his health and wellbeing by retiring for good after two failed attempts.

Peter previously trained Fury between 2011 and 2017, but left the camp amid a schism with father and son.

The Gypsy King had previously sought to set the record straight on Peter's involvement with his rival on social media, deeming Joshua's comments 'categorically untrue'.

'Even if Peter Fury hated me, he’s still my family,' he said. 'That would mean he would be a Fredo, scorpion, snake, rat, b****** piece of s*** if he did that.'

Sports.title: Boxing chief Turki Alalshikh calls out Dua Lipa in bizarre rant about pop sensation during Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua press conference
Sports.content:
Boxing chief Turki Alalshikh has claimed that Dua Lipa has refused to perform at the Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua super-fight in a bizarre tirade against the pop sensation during the launch press conference.

On Wednesday evening, Britain's two most iconic boxers of the last two decades went face to face for the first time since their eagerly anticipated clash was announced last week.

Ahead of the press conference, Alalshikh, who was lauded by Fury, Joshua and many others during the evening for financing the fight, was invited to speak about how the 'Battle of Britain' came to be.

New York's Madison Square Garden and Wembley had previously been billed as potential venues for the 'super' heavyweight clash, but it has since been confirmed that the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales, will host the contest.

During his explanation of how the venue was eventually decided, Alalshikh took a swipe at Dua Lipa in the process.

He said: 'I will be honest today, I know that London wouldn't give me the stadium until 2am, and I know that Dua Lipa will not perform in the stadium, because she doesn't like boxing, and maybe she doesn't like me.'

Turki Alalshikh went on a bizarre tirade during Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua press conference

The boxing chief claimed that Dua Lipa has turned down the chance to perform ahead of the long-awaited bout

Dua Lipa's representatives have been approached for comment by Daily Mail Sport.

Alalshikh went on to also explain the financial losses that staging the bout in Britain has led to.

He added: 'Nobody questioned me about UK. I love the British people, I try to deliver everything for them. Put yourself in my shoes; there's a situation to lose $70million (£52.8m); the best is to have it in a good time zone.

'I have two reasons, and I know London won't deliver it; they won't give me the stadium until 2am... Wales delivered it; it's still the UK, the town of Ryan Giggs, let's do it.'

Anthony Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has been vocal about his and the two-time heavyweight world champion's desire to have the fight staged in the UK.

The chairman of Matchroom took his moment on stage at the British Airways ARC to thank the British boxing community for applying the 'pressure' to ensure the fight is played out on British soil.

Fury and Joshua faced off for the first time ahead of their super fight on Wednesday evening

'I'm excited,' Hearn said. 'Turki, I know we've fallen out, but I promise you this'll be the greatest night you've ever had in boxing.

'On a serious note, when we talked about this fight, you envisaged it for British boxing. This guy (Joshua) has changed boxing in this country. So has Tyson Fury. We are the envy of the boxing world.

'We can't stage it anywhere else. Thank you to the British public for putting the pressure on. We couldn't do it, we failed.'

Sports.title: Ricky Hatton left £30MILLION estate after his tragic death, new figures reveal, as son Campbell claims family are 'completely in the dark' amid dispute over late boxer's finances
Sports.content:
Ricky Hatton left £30MILLION estate after his tragic death, new figures reveal, as son Campbell claims family are 'completely in the dark' amid dispute over late boxer's finances

Ricky Hatton reportedly amassed a £30million fortune before his death last year, though uncertainty remains over how the boxing legend's estate will be distributed.

Hatton, who died aged 46 last September, won multiple world titles before using his fight earnings to build a business empire worth more than £20million, with at least another £10m tied up in property investments, according to The Sun.

Trustees were appointed to manage Hatton's estate after he took his own life in September last year.

However, sources close to the family claim communication with the trustees has since broken down, with one describing the situation as a 'complete mess', according to an earlier report in The Sun.

It was thought Hatton had intended for his fortune to pass to his three children, Campbell, 25, and daughters Millie, 14, and Fearne, 12. However, a year after his death, the family are still waiting to learn how and when the estate will be distributed.

Campbell told The Sun on Wednesday: 'My family is still completely in the dark. We’ve had no involvement in my dad’s finances for over 15 years.'

Hatton, who died aged 46 last September, won multiple world titles before using his fight earnings to build a business and property empire

It was thought Hatton had intended for his fortune to pass to his three children, Campbell, 25 (above), and daughters Millie, 14, and Fearne, 12

During his successful boxing career, Hatton used his fight earnings to finance a string of businesses, many of them linked to property investments in his hometown of Hyde, as well as in Leicestershire, London and Kent.

One source said Hatton was 'determined to ensure that he had a financial legacy from his incredible career'.

'Everyone who knew and loved Ricky would give anything to have him back. But during his life he's done a great job of providing for the people he loved the most, his children,' the source added.

Earlier this month, the Daily Mail reported that Hatton's house had been sold for £1.5m this year after £350,000 was knocked off the original asking price.

The house, where Hatton was found in September last year, was put up for sale shortly before his death for £1.85million but was later taken off the market following his tragic death.

The mansion then went back on offer for £1.75million, then £1.65million before it was sold for £1.5million.

It was described by the estate agent as being a 'landmark modern residence offering luxury, space and unrivalled lifestyle features'.

It said that the five-bedroom six-bathroom property, which was built in 2010, had been 'impeccably designed'.

Earlier this month, the Daily Mail reported that Hatton's house had been sold for £1.5m this year after £350,000 was knocked off the original asking price

One source said Hatton was 'determined to ensure that he had a financial legacy from his incredible career'

Hatton put his own stamp on the property, decorating it with personal touches including a traditional telephone box in the garden and an array of Manchester City memorabilia. Among its more unusual features are seats salvaged from the club's former Maine Road stadium.

It has extensive landscaped grounds with greenbelt views, plus a leisure suite with a heated indoor pool and jacuzzi.

A private gym and cinema room complement a games room and bar area, which is separated from the pool by a striking glass wall.

The principal bedroom suite features a walk-in dressing room, a luxurious en suite bathroom, a crushed-velvet chaise longue and dark patterned wallpaper.

Elsewhere, the property offers multiple reception rooms and expansive open-plan living areas centred around a high-specification, dark-panelled kitchen.

Situated in the sought-after area of Gee Cross in Greater Manchester, the estate is equipped with advanced security features, including CCTV.

The estate agents said: 'This is a rare opportunity to acquire a truly outstanding home in one of the North West's most prestigious and sought-after residential locations.'
