Sports.title: Whittaker Holds On To Beat Wallace
Sports.content:
Ben “The Surgeon” Whittaker survived a difficult finish to defeat Conor Wallace by unanimous decision over 12 rounds at Utilita Arena in Birmingham on Saturday. The Matchroom Boxing card, promoted by Eddie Hearn, aired on DAZN.

Whittaker (13-0-1, 9 KOs), the Tokyo Olympic silver medalist from Darlaston, retained his WBC Silver light heavyweight title and secured the IBF mandatory position. Wallace (17-2, 12 KOs), a Northern Irish-born southpaw based in Brisbane, made him work hard to protect the lead he had built.

Whittaker controlled most of the first nine rounds before Wallace hurt him with a lead left to the chin in the tenth. Wallace’s success made the closing rounds increasingly difficult, although Whittaker steadied himself in the 11th.

In the 12th, Wallace hurt Whittaker badly and pressed for a stoppage. Whittaker repeatedly held and struggled to stay upright, with referee Kieran McCann separating the fighters as the home boxer tried to reach the bell. Several falls prompted questions about whether knockdowns should have been called, but none were officially recorded.

Whittaker won by scores of 117-111, 116-112 and 115-113. His early work secured the victory, but Wallace’s late attack exposed defensive weaknesses that will need attention before a world title fight.

Bilal Fawaz stops Eithan James

British and Commonwealth junior middleweight champion Bilal Fawaz (13-1-1, 5 KOs), of London, retained his titles by stopping Northampton’s Eithan James (17-3) at 1:14 of the eighth round of their scheduled 12-round contest.

Fawaz dropped James with a right hand to the chin, then scored another knockdown before referee Ron Kearney ended the fight. James suffered his first stoppage defeat, while Fawaz collected the £5,000 knockout bonus Hearn had offered before the bout.

Hamza Uddin takes Sean Bruce’s British title

Walsall’s Hamza “The Great” Uddin (8-0, 5 KOs) stopped British flyweight champion Sean Bruce (8-3), of Leicester, at 2:49 of round eight to claim the British and vacant Commonwealth titles.

Uddin scored two knockdowns in the fifth round, with Bruce beating referee Victor Loughlin’s counts and continuing to fight. A third knockdown, from a body shot in the eighth, ended the contest. Loughlin waved it off immediately, bringing Bruce’s first British title defense to a close.

Ibraheem Sulaimaan retains English title

Birmingham southpaw Ibraheem “Spider” Sulaimaan defeated Sonny Hardy (12-1, 5 KOs), of Wickford, by unanimous decision after 10 competitive rounds to retain his English super featherweight title.

There was little between them after six rounds, and referee Chris Dean deducted a point from Sulaimaan in the seventh. The champion finished strongly over the final three rounds to secure scores of 97-93, 97-93 and 96-93.

Hardy’s work in the middle rounds made the contest closer than the cards suggested to some ringside observers, with several scoring it narrowly and others favoring the challenger.

Aaron Bowen wins Midlands Area title

Aaron Bowen (9-1, 6 KOs), of Coventry, took the Midlands Area super middleweight title from Klinton Baptiste (5-1) by unanimous decision over 10 rounds.

Bowen repeatedly landed lead right hands from the third round onward, leaving Baptiste’s left eye badly swollen and nearly closed. Baptiste absorbed sustained punishment but lasted the distance as Bowen pursued a stoppage.

The scores were 99-91, 99-92 and 98-92.

Odel Kamara wins professional debut

Liverpool junior middleweight Odel “King” Kamara (1-0, 1 KO), a 2025 World Boxing champion, stopped Greece’s Thodoris Ritzakis (5-6-1) at 2:53 of the third round of their scheduled four-round bout.

Kamara dropped Ritzakis in the opening round, with referee Ryan Churchill administering an eight-count. In the third, Kamara landed a short uppercut in close before Churchill called a halt, with Ritzakis bleeding from the nose.

The stoppage drew criticism from some ringside observers for being premature. Kamara also looked tired early and left openings while loading up on power shots, making this a successful debut with room for improvement.

Harley Burrows stops Matias Ezequiel Herrera

Harley “The Beast” Burrows (3-0, 2 KOs) stopped Argentina’s Matias Ezequiel Herrera (8-9-2, 5 KOs) at 1:24 of round two in a scheduled six-round middleweight contest.

Burrows pressured Herrera and mixed punches to the head and body. With Herrera pinned against the ropes under a sustained attack, referee Ryan Churchill stepped in to end the fight.

Adam Maca overwhelms Rogger Rivera

Adam “The Mac” Maca (7-0, 6 KOs), an Albanian super featherweight based in Brighton, stopped Peru’s Rogger Rivera (3-6, 2 KOs) at 2:56 of round two in their scheduled six-round bout.

Maca overwhelmed Rivera with power shots until referee Chris Dean intervened. The 19-year-old produced another quick finish, suggesting he is ready for opposition that can offer more resistance.

Paige Murray edges Linzi Buczynskyj

Paige “Perfect” Murray (5-0), of Leicester, defeated Bolton’s Linzi Buczynskyj (6-13) over four two-minute rounds.

Murray controlled the opening round but had a point deducted by referee Chris Dean in the second for repeatedly pulling down Buczynskyj’s head. She won the third and fourth rounds to secure a 38-37 decision.

David Diamante served as the ring announcer.

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker Beats Conor Wallace After Late Scare
Sports.content:
Ben Whittaker (13-0-1) survived a desperate final round to defeat Conor Wallace (17-2) by unanimous decision tonight at Utilita Arena in Birmingham, securing the IBF mandatory position at light heavyweight. Whittaker retained his WBC Silver title, but the closing minutes raised questions about his readiness for a world championship fight.

The judges scored it 117-111, 116-112 and 115-113. No knockdowns were officially recorded, although Whittaker’s falls during Wallace’s final-round assault became a disputed part of the result.

Whittaker controlled most of the first nine rounds, building the lead that ultimately protected his unbeaten record. Wallace could not collect enough rounds early, leaving the Northern Irish-born Australian southpaw needing a dramatic turnaround down the stretch.

He began finding more success in the tenth. With his feet planted, Wallace landed shots that disrupted Whittaker’s rhythm, while the home fighter complained to the referee. Whittaker recovered to take the 11th before Wallace launched his strongest attack in the final round.

Wallace hurt Whittaker and pursued the stoppage, forcing him to grab, stumble and wrestle his way through the remaining time. At one point, Whittaker tackled Wallace as he struggled to stay upright.

Bad Left Hook scored the round 10-8 for Wallace and argued that two or three knockdowns could have been called. Those calls never came, and Whittaker reached the bell with his earlier work enough to secure the decision.

The concern for Whittaker is how little control he had once Wallace hurt him. Holding bought him time, but he struggled to regain his balance or produce enough offense to discourage the pursuit. A stronger finisher could make that escape much harder.

Wallace deserves credit for continuing to press after losing much of the early action. His late surge fell short, but it exposed vulnerabilities that Whittaker and trainer Andy Lee need to address before pursuing the IBF belt held by Dmitry Bivol.

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker vs. Conor Wallace Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Ben Whittaker (13-0-1) survived a punishing final round to defeat Conor Wallace (17-2) by unanimous decision, retaining his WBC Silver light heavyweight title and securing the IBF mandatory position for Dmitry Bivol’s belt. The scores were 117-111, 116-112 and 115-113 after 12 rounds in Birmingham.

Whittaker controlled much of the early action, but Wallace hurt him badly in the 12th, leaving him grabbing and struggling to stay upright. No knockdowns were officially scored, although several falls drew criticism over whether Wallace should have received knockdown calls during his late push for a stoppage.

Undercard results

Odel Kamara (1-0) stopped Thodoris Ritzakis (5-6-1) in round three of his professional debut tonight in Birmingham, landing a short uppercut before the referee waved it off. Eddie Hearn rates the 22-year-old junior middleweight highly, but Kamara looked wild swinging for the fences and took unnecessary punches from his overmatched opponent.

The stoppage drew ringside criticism for being premature, and Kamara’s power looked less impressive than the result suggests. At 5’8″, he could be better suited to welterweight, although his stocky build leaves a question over whether he can comfortably make 147 pounds.

Hamza Uddin (8-0) stopped Sean Bruce (8-3) at 2:49 of round eight to capture the British flyweight title and vacant Commonwealth belt at Utilita Arena in Birmingham. The 23-year-old from Walsall scored three knockdowns, finishing Bruce with a body shot near the ropes.

Bruce doubled over and went down, prompting referee Victor Loughlin to wave off the contest without starting a count. Uddin picked apart the champion with accurate punching, producing an impressive performance in his first British title fight. Bruce lost his belt in his first defense and could not withstand Uddin’s precision or sustained attack.

Bilal Fawaz (13-1-1) retained his British and Commonwealth junior middleweight titles by stopping Eithan James (17-3) at 1:14 of round eight in Birmingham. A heavy right hand sent James to the canvas near the ropes, and another knockdown brought the referee’s intervention.

The 38-year-old Fawaz delivered the finish just as commentary suggested he was beginning to feel the pace. James suffered his first stoppage defeat, while Fawaz earned the £5,000 knockout bonus Eddie Hearn had offered before the fight.

English super featherweight champion Ibraheem Sulaimaan retained his title with a hard-fought unanimous decision over Sonny Hardy after 10 rounds at Utilita Arena Birmingham. The scores were 97–93, 97–93 and 96–93, moving the Birmingham southpaw to 12–0 and handing Hardy his first defeat at 12–1.

Sulaimaan started quickly, but Hardy pushed him through a difficult stretch in the middle rounds, knocking his gumshield out during one exchange. The champion also had a point deducted before recovering his momentum in the eighth and finishing strongly over the final three rounds. Several ringside observers scored the contest considerably closer than the official judges, with some favoring Hardy.

Aaron Bowen (9-1) captured the Midlands Area super middleweight title with a unanimous decision over Klinton Baptiste (5-1) at Utilita Arena in Birmingham. The scores were 99-91, 99-92 and 98-92 after 10 rounds.

Bowen controlled the fight, catching Baptiste with clean right hands against the ropes and pressing for a stoppage. Baptiste fought with one eye closed for roughly half the contest but lasted the distance without a reported knockdown.

The punishment prompted ringside criticism that his corner should have intervened, although his durability kept Bowen from securing the finish. Bowen earned a clear victory, while Baptiste’s resistance made the closing rounds harder than the wide scores might suggest. Baptiste looked gone on a couple of occasions, but surprisingly, he stayed in there.

Super featherweight Adam Maca (7-0, 6 KOs) stopped Rogger Rivera (3-6, 2 KOs) at 2:56 of round two in their scheduled six-round contest. The 19-year-old unloaded with power shots until referee Chris Dean stepped in to end the fight. It was Maca’s sixth stoppage in seven professional outings.

The teenager produced another impressive finish, but he is making this level of opposition look too easy. Rivera offered little opportunity to assess how Maca handles resistance or adjusts when his power alone cannot settle a fight. Maca looks ready for better opposition that can extend him and give him more to solve.

Harley Burrows stopped Matias Ezequiel Herrera at 1:24 of round two in their scheduled six-round middleweight contest on the Ben Whittaker–Conor Wallace undercard in Birmingham. The 20-year-old southpaw pressured Herrera from the opening bell, mixing punches to the head and body.

Burrows trapped the Argentine against the ropes in the second round and punched through his high guard until referee Ryan Churchill intervened. Herrera had not been knocked down before the stoppage, which drew some ringside criticism for being slightly early. Burrows’ attack was wild at times, but his sustained pressure kept Herrera struggling to find room to respond.

The DAZN broadcast starts at 2:00 p.m. ET / 7:00 p.m. UK, with a subscription required. That is the card’s start time; Whittaker and Wallace fight later in the evening.

Whittaker has a chance to move within reach of a world title shot, but he must first get through Wallace over the scheduled 12 rounds. British title fights involving Sean Bruce and Bilal Fawaz feature on the undercard.

Sports.title: Odel Kamara Wins Debut But Looks Gassed In Three
Sports.content:
Odel Kamara (1-0) won his professional debut with a third-round stoppage of Thodoris Ritzakis (5-6-1) tonight at Utilita Arena in Birmingham, but the junior middleweight prospect looked raw despite the quick finish.

Promoter Eddie Hearn has high hopes for the 22-year-old Liverpool fighter. Against Ritzakis, however, Kamara swung for the fences, left himself open, and took punches from an opponent brought in to give him a successful start.

The finish came with Ritzakis near the ropes. After the fighters clinched and the referee moved in, Kamara landed a short uppercut in close, prompting an immediate wave-off. No official stoppage time was available.

Matchroom talked up the uppercut, but ringside observers viewed the stoppage as early. The Sweet Science called it a gift, though another outlet credited Kamara with an opening-round knockdown to applaud his debut.

Kamara secured the win, but his power didn’t look threatening against this caliber of opponent. He threw full force into his punches without generating serious pop. Overcommitting on those big swings only opened the door for Ritzakis to counter him cleanly.

That is something Kamara needs to address before the opposition gets better. A stronger junior middleweight could punish those openings much more severely, especially if Kamara cannot discourage him with his punching power. Shorter combinations and a quicker return to his guard would give him a more reliable approach.

His height presents another question. At 5’8″, Kamara will often be giving away reach at 154 pounds, making his entries particularly important. He cannot afford to rush forward throwing wide shots against taller fighters who can catch him coming in.

Welterweight looks like the better weight class for Kamara, yet his thick frame raises questions about whether he can squeeze down to 147 without draining himself. For now, learning to keep his hands up matters far more than hunting for another quick knockout.

Far more alarming was how quickly Kamara faded. By round three, he looked like he was running on empty, exposing glaring conditioning problems even factoring in first-fight adrenaline and the leap from three-round amateur sprints.

Loading up on every single punch clearly drained his tank, substituting wild, explosive swings for controlled rhythm. Put him in with a tough veteran capable of taking those shots and firing back, and that premature fatigue will get him stopped well before the final bell.

Sports.title: Bilal Fawaz Stops Eithan James In Eight Rounds
Sports.content:
Bilal Fawaz (13-1-1) retained his British and Commonwealth junior middleweight titles with an eighth-round stoppage of Eithan James (17-3) tonight at Utilita Arena in Birmingham. The finish came at 1:14 of the round, earning the 38-year-old champion the £5,000 knockout bonus Eddie Hearn had offered before the fight.

Fawaz landed a heavy right hand that dropped James near the ropes, then scored another knockdown before the referee ended the contest. For James, it was his first stoppage defeat, with all his previous professional fights having gone to decisions.

The ending came almost immediately after commentator Darren Barker suggested Fawaz was feeling the pace. That observation offered James some encouragement, but Fawaz still had enough power to end the fight suddenly. Any prospect of the younger challenger taking advantage of a tiring champion disappeared with the right hand.

James, 26, entered with considerably more experience going the distance than dealing with a fight-ending crisis. His record showed he could complete rounds, but Fawaz forced a different test in the eighth. Once the champion hurt him, James could not get through the follow-up and recover between rounds.

For Fawaz, the result gives him a successful defense against a challenger 12 years younger. His age will remain part of the discussion when tougher opponents arrive, particularly if he begins to tire during longer fights. Against James, however, he retained the punching power to settle the contest before it reached the championship rounds.

Hearn’s bonus added a financial reward to the finish, although keeping both titles was the larger achievement. Fawaz left Birmingham with his belts after turning a moment when his stamina was being questioned into the decisive attack.

James now has a different kind of defeat to recover from. Previous points losses allowed him to finish the fight; this time, Fawaz’s power took that option away.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Expects Teofimo Lopez To Abandon Title
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez could give up his WBA welterweight title to pursue Ryan Garcia rather than fight Jack Catterall. Tim Bradley expects him to choose the bigger payday, viewing Catterall’s southpaw style as a dangerous obstacle to that opportunity.

Lopez has until the close of business Eastern Time on October 22 to reach an agreement with Catterall. The WBA ordered the fight on September 22 between its “super” champion Teofimo and “regular” champion Catterall, who is also the mandatory challenger.

Bradley doubts Teofimo will take that route.

“Hell yeah he gonna duck,” Bradley said during a panel discussion at Sean Zittel and 2 more on YouTube. “Jack Catterall fight is a hard fight for him. I think that’s a hard fight. It’s another southpaw … that jab, Catterall jab, good counterpunching. Teo got to go look for him.”

That is the difficulty Bradley identifies: Teofimo would have to create the exchanges against someone comfortable waiting to counter. Chasing Catterall could leave him reaching with punches and entering off balance, giving the challenger opportunities to score and move before Lopez can answer.

Ryan offers a different incentive. His name would help sell the event, and Teofimo could pursue that payday without first risking a defeat against Catterall. Bradley suggests Teofimo could decide to abandon the belt if that is what it takes to get Ryan.

However, October 22 is a negotiation deadline, rather than an automatic date for Teofimo to lose his championship. If the camps cannot agree, or either side walks away, the WBA can order a purse bid. Bradley’s prediction goes further, anticipating that Lopez will ultimately choose Ryan over fulfilling the mandatory.

Giving up the title would also remove a potential belt from the Ryan matchup. Lopez would be trading his position as champion for the earning potential of the opponent.

For Catterall, the immediate question is whether Teofimo will negotiate the ordered defense. For Teofimo, Bradley sees a choice between protecting a lucrative opportunity and taking a fight that could spoil it.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Seeks Shakur Fight To Answer Doubters
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield wants to make Shakur fight through pain, targeting his arms and shoulders when clean head shots aren’t available. His proposed approach is to punish the defense itself until openings appear.

There’s an understandable reason Schofield wants this fight so badly. Their canceled February 2025 meeting left him facing accusations that he wanted out. For fans who still suspect he feigned illness, another callout won’t settle anything. Getting into the ring with Shakur would give him the opportunity to answer them.

Schofield was reported ill and hospitalized before that scheduled fight. That does not establish that he fabricated an illness to avoid Shakur.

“That’s who I want before I finish my career,” Schofield told Fight Hub TV about Shakur. “I’m throwing to break bones. Like I ain’t even going to lie, in sparring I was practicing like breaking shoulders. Like I was hitting shoulders, hitting like forearms. I was just hitting anywhere I can. You know, I don’t care.”

The thinking is straightforward: if Shakur makes his head difficult to hit, Schofield wants to make blocking punches costly. Sustained attacks to the arms could make holding the guard and returning punches harder as the rounds progress.

Executing that against Shakur would require more than aggression. Schofield would need to cut off his exits, stay balanced while punching, and avoid spending entire rounds striking the guard while taking clean counters. He also argues that opponents need several approaches, recognizing that pressure alone might not be enough.

First comes Lucas Bahdi. Schofield’s next fight is scheduled for October 10 in Chicago for the vacant WBA lightweight title, giving him an immediate opportunity to advance his championship ambitions.

Schofield acknowledges Bahdi’s patience and knockout power but wants a stoppage himself. That ambition brings its own danger: forcing a finish could create the opening Bahdi needs.

Beating Bahdi would strengthen Schofield’s position to pursue bigger fights. Settling the doubts surrounding Shakur still requires a fight that actually happens.

Sports.title: Agit Kabayel Ticket Sales Revive The Klitschko Blueprint
Sports.content:
Agit Kabayel’s reported 25,000 presale ticket sales give Frank Warren a financial reason to continue arranging manageable defenses in Germany. If Nelson Hysa attracts that level of demand, tougher opposition becomes less urgent from a business perspective.

The November 28 fight in Düsseldorf offers an early indication that Kabayel’s popularity can sell a stadium event without an established heavyweight rival.

“25,000 tickets sold in 24 hours presale for Agit Kabayel vs Nelson Hysa in Germany next month!” Warren posted on X. “Presale still open for the World Heavyweight title fight not to be missed.”

There are echoes of the Klitschko approach: build the evening around the champion, with the challenger supplying an unbeaten record and an optimistic knockout promise. Wladimir’s defense against Francesco Pianeta in Mannheim demonstrated how a less accomplished opponent could become part of a major German boxing occasion.

Warren’s figures suggest Kabayel may be developing similar commercial freedom. Overseas criticism of Hysa’s credentials has less financial consequence if local supporters keep buying seats.

That would represent a change from the fights that established Kabayel internationally. He stopped Arslanbek Makhmudov and Frank Sanchez in Riyadh, beating unbeaten contenders whose reputations made those victories meaningful. Those performances supplied evidence of his ability under pressure.

Hysa, 25-0 with 23 knockouts, offers attractive promotional numbers. At 42, however, he faces a substantial increase in opposition. Beating him would provide Kabayel with another successful defense while revealing comparatively little about his chances against the other champions.

The business calculation also extends beyond the stadium. DAZN lists the event as pay-per-view. German ticket buyers may embrace a homecoming spectacle, while international viewers could require a more competitive matchup before paying. No broadcast sales figures are available to establish that demand.

A profitable German base could help Kabayel negotiate better terms for future unifications, including offers from Saudi Arabia. He would have a credible alternative to accepting whatever purse is offered abroad.

The sporting cost comes if comfortable defenses become the routine. Kabayel has already shown he can beat dangerous contenders. Spending more of his prime proving he can sell tickets would delay the fights needed to establish how far that ability can take him.

Ghana News.title: NPP Delegates conference: The wisdom of the masses will prevail – Napo
Ghana News.content:
Dr Matthew Opoku Prempeh , NPP Running Mate

The New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) 2024 running mate, Dr Matthew Opoku Prempeh, has expressed confidence in the party’s delegates to make the right choices as they vote in the party’s national executive elections.

Dr Opoku Prempeh, popularly known as Napo, said the outcome of the elections should be determined by delegates, stressing that the democratic process within the party must be respected.

Speaking in an interview during the NPP National Delegates Conference in Kumasi on Saturday, 3 October, Dr Opoku Prempeh said he had no personal interest in influencing the outcome of the elections and was leaving the decision entirely in the hands of delegates.

“The wisdom of the masses will prevail,” he said when asked about the elections being held during the conference.

He said delegates from across the country had gathered to participate in an important democratic exercise that would help shape the future direction of the party.

According to him, every vote cast would contribute to determining the leadership of the NPP and strengthening the party as it prepares for future elections.

Dr Opoku Prempeh also commented on the NPP’s prospects ahead of the 2028 general election, acknowledging the competitive nature of elections in Ghana.

“All Ghana's elections have been tough and have been keenly contested, but at the end of the day, the wisdom of the masses will speak,” he said.

He expressed confidence in the NPP’s future electoral prospects and voiced his support for Dr Mahamudu Bawumia’s political ambitions.

“The voters will decide who they think will give Ghana hope from 2029 onward, and they will elect that person. And I believe sincerely, it's going to be Dr Mahamudu Bawumia and the NPP,” he said.

He commended the conduct of party supporters, delegates and candidates throughout the conference, describing their participation in the internal electoral process as encouraging.

Ghana News.title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says
Ghana News.content:
The co-pilot who attempted to take control of a Flydubai plane travelling to Israel attacked the pilot with a crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said.

The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv carrying more than 170 people plunged 17,000ft (5,200m) two and a half hours into its journey, before passengers managed to overpower the attacker and successfully take control of the plane.

Capt Smit Machchhar said he was lying on the floor injured when he realised the plane was sinking and he had to act, explaining: "I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside", which allowed the passengers in.

Two reserve pilots then landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia.

A crash axe is usually kept in the cockpit in case of an emergency.

The weapon used has been a key question for investigators, given the stringent security on such a sensitive route. Early reports from passengers on board had suggested it might have been a knife.

The UAE attorney general told state media that investigations were ongoing to determine the full circumstances and motives of the incident.

The co-pilot who launched the attack was an Omani national, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Multiple media outlets, including Reuters, CNN and The New York Times, have named him as Hamam al-Hammami. There has been no official confirmation of this.

While working at another airline, Oman Air, US media reported that Al-Hammami was removed from flight training due to concerns about his radical views and was given another role at Oman's national airline.

He completed a three-year distance-learning course at Buckinghamshire New University in the UK and graduated with a degree in aviation management in 2023, the university said. It added that he did not take any pilot training at the school.

Speaking to Fox News, Netanyahu said that after the attacker was subdued on the flight, he called out to the crew, "Kill me, kill me!"

The Israeli prime minister added: "So, it's clear that he was suicidal… It looks very likely that he was going to bring the plane down."

He also said the attacker "underwent Islamist radical indoctrination".

The UAE's attorney general, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, said investigations into the incident revealed that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a "terrorist act", according to the country's state news agency.

He also said investigations were underway to establish the circumstances, motives, and any links related to the incident.

Machchhar, who was stabbed in the attack, was taken to a nearby hospital before being airlifted to Abu Dhabi, where he is reported to be in a stable condition.

The pilot, who is from India, was in "good health and recovering well", the Indian embassy in the UAE said on Thursday.

"I am confident that the recovery will be there and I will become fit and healthy again," Machchhar said.

About two and a half hours after the plane took off from Dubai International Airport, it began to plunge sharply.

The plane signalled a "general emergency" code, squawk 7700, before switching to squawk 7500, a code reporting "unlawful interference", or hijacking.

In an interview with the BBC, one passenger described the moment he realised that something was wrong.

Almog Itali said: "Suddenly the aeroplane started to, like a rollercoaster, to drop down [with] a massive G-force. It was falling down for 20 or 30 seconds, rapidly, and then balanced, and then started once again to fall down."

People then began to rush to the cockpit, he said.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog said on Thursday that the alarm was raised onboard by an Israeli woman, Tali Manes, who heard a commotion coming from the cockpit.

Her husband, Zvika, along with three other men - Yaniv Hayun, Dr Shota Musayev and Asaf Rajuan - entered the cockpit after Capt Machchhar managed to open the door despite his injuries.

Hayun said, in a video released by the prime minister's office, that the attacker was "trying to destroy the instruments in order to disable the plane".

Hayun then described putting the attacker in a chokehold and pulling him outside the cockpit before other passengers helped to pin him down.

He added that he "pulled the controls" of the plane. "The plane started to level out, a bit more, and then [another] pilot told me he was taking control from there," he said.

In an interview with CNN on Wednesday evening, Netanyahu said the stabbed pilot, passengers and second crew had "managed to prevent a 9/11 disaster".

The New Patriotic Party (NPP) Constituency Chairman for Bosome Freho in the Ashanti Region, Patrick Kwaku Frimpong, has reportedly been arrested by the Ghana Police Service following an alleged incident involving a ballot paper at the party’s National Delegates Conference.

Reports say the incident occurred after a delegate from the constituency encountered difficulties with the electronic voting system and was unable to cast a ballot.

The Ashanti Regional Secretary of the NPP, Dr Francis Adomako, had reportedly earlier written to the constituency to bar the delegate from participating in Saturday’s election.

However, after the delegate experienced difficulties with the electoral system, the Electoral Commission (EC) reportedly issued a ballot paper to allow the individual to vote.

The constituency chairman is alleged to have taken the ballot paper and torn it apart.

The incident reportedly prompted the police to arrest Mr Frimpong for questioning.

Further details on the circumstances surrounding the incident and whether any charges have been filed were not immediately available.

Ghana News.title: Medical plane with 6 on board missing off Massachusetts coast
Ghana News.content:
The search for the plane is being conducted near Nantucket, an island off the coast of the US state of Massachusetts

US authorities are searching for six people after a medical plane bound for Boston, Massachusetts, went missing early Saturday morning.

The Federal Aviation Administration told the BBC that it lost contact with the Gulfstream G-100 and issued a search-and-rescue notice just after 1:00 local time (6:00 GMT).

An air and water search is underway off the coast of Nantucket, a Massachusetts island, according to the US Coast Guard's Northeast District.

The plane departed from Bermuda's L.F. Wade International Airport at 23:40 local time, according to FlightAware data, and was scheduled to land at Boston's Logan International Airport at 1:30 EDT (6:30 GMT).

According to the tail number released by the Coast Guard, the plane belonged to Latitude Air Ambulances, a company that provides international medical flights for patients returning home.

Among those on board were two pilots and two medical staff, both Canadian, Clarence Togeretz, director of flight operations at Latitude, told CBC News.

The crew flew to Bermuda to collect a patient and their relative, who are not Canadian, Togeretz said.

FlightAware's tracker shows the aircraft significantly dropped in altitude before its communications went dark, plummeting from around 7,300m (24,000ft) to 3,300m (11,000ft).

Radio transmissions show trouble with communications between the air traffic controller and the pilot, the Boston Globe reported based on transmissions provided by LiveATC.net.

"You're coming in blind? Is that what you said?" the air traffic controller asked. "Are you declaring an emergency, or no?"

The pilot's response was inaudible.

"You're coming in a little weak, so I didn't hear what your response was, if you were declaring an emergency or not," the air traffic controller said, according to the Globe.

The air traffic controller later confirmed the pilot had declared an emergency.

An area fire dispatcher asked emergency crews just after 1:00 EDT to prepare to meet a plane with an "electrical issue".

The dispatcher later said, "The aircraft has lost radio and radar".

Ghana News.title: Bolt driver jailed 25 years for robbing beautician
Ghana News.content:
An Adenta Circuit Court has sentenced a 22-year-old motor mechanic to 25 years’ imprisonment in hard labour for robbing a beautician.

Emmanuel Kofi Mensah, who is also a Bolt driver, slashed the complainant’s wrist and little finger with a cutlass before robbing her of two iPhones, valued at GH¢18,000 and GH¢3,500, cash of GH¢3,200, and other personal belongings.

The robbery occurred at Mantey Farms, Adenta, on September 23, 2026, at about 2200 hours, when the complainant, Yvonne Dzane Dzifa, hired Mensah’s services.

Mensah, who was charged with robbery, pleaded guilty.

The Court, presided over by Mrs Angela Attachie, convicted Mensah on his own plea and sentenced him accordingly.

The prosecution, led by Chief Inspector Maxwell Lanyo, said Dzifa, a beautician, resided at Adenta New Site.

It said Mensah, now a convict, was a motor mechanic and also resided at Adenta New Site.

On September 23, at about 2200 hours, the complainant boarded Mensah’s Bolt vehicle at Madina Zongo Junction, heading to Adenta.

When they arrived at her destination at Adenta Barrier, the complainant prompted Mensah to stop so she could alight, but he failed to stop, locked all the doors, and drove towards the Adenta-Dodowa road.

Prosecution said the complainant sensed danger and shouted for help, but no one could hear her.

The Prosecutor said Mensah drove to a location at Mantey Farms along the Adenta-Dodowa road, where he stopped and attacked the complainant.

Mensah demanded that the complainant hand over her handbag and other belongings, but she refused.

The prosecution said that, infuriated, Mensah pulled out a cutlass from the vehicle and threatened to harm her if she resisted.

The Court heard that Mensah pulled the complainant from the vehicle onto the ground and repeatedly hit her with the cutlass in an attempt to force her to surrender her bag.

The complainant continued to resist and held firmly onto her bag.

After a fierce struggle, Mensah slashed her left wrist and little finger with the cutlass and succeeded in taking her bag, which contained an iPhone 17 Pro Max valued at GH¢18,000, an iPhone 12 valued at GH¢3,500, cash of GH¢3,200 and other personal effects.

Prosecution said Mensah then called an accomplice, who was at large, and the accomplice arrived on a motorbike to assist him.

The complainant managed to grab a backpack from the vehicle's front seat and fled into a nearby bush.

Mensah and his accomplice chased her with the cutlass in an attempt to retrieve the backpack, but were unsuccessful.

Prosecution said the complainant scaled the fence wall of a nearby house and sought refuge in the compound until the following morning, when the landlord informed the Police of her presence.

The Police visited the location and rescued the complainant. A search of the backpack revealed a tablet and a mini-laptop believed to be stolen property.

Prosecution said the complainant, who had sustained a deep cutlass wound to her left wrist and little finger, as well as bruises all over her body, formally reported the incident to the Police.

She was issued a medical report form and attended the Pantang Government Hospital, where she was treated and discharged.

On September 24, at about 1300 hours, Mensah sent the iPhone 17 Pro Max to an Apple shop at Madina Zongo Junction for sale.

While inspecting the phone, the shop owner saw the complainant’s picture on it and suspected that it had been stolen. Prosecution said the shop owner caused Mensah’s arrest and handed him over to the Police.

A search conducted on him revealed the same cutlass he allegedly used in the attack, concealed in his shorts. The prosecution said Mensah admitted the offence in his caution statement and pleaded for forgiveness.

The Court heard that Mensah had informed the Police that the Bolt vehicle belonged to a Nigerian friend, but he had since failed to identify the friend and the other accomplice involved in the robbery.

Prosecution said efforts were underway to identify the accomplices and arrest them to face the law.

Ghana News.title: Happy 76th Birthday to the Daily Graphic!
Ghana News.content:
The 2nd of October should be celebrated as one of the really pivotal days in the history of the media in Ghana.

For that day in 1950 saw the birth of a technologically advanced method of producing newspapers in the country,

then known as the Gold Coast.

It wasn't only in the printing domain that the Graphic shone (being a slick, pictorial "tabloid" in the midst of fairly stodgy broadsheets). The content was also revolutionary. Instead of long articles devoted largely to the opinions of the country's elite, the paper was full of crisp news reports, each carrying the byline of a living person. Names like S.N. Addo, Anthony Mensah et al.

Photographs were, aside hinted earlier, generously sprinkled throughout the entire paper. It had a special sports section, again dominated by people with bylines, saying what they thought of the football clubs of the time and their stars!

But above all else, there were the feature articles, written by writers who had a marvellous command of the English language, and could educate and entertain at the same time: Moses Danquah, Bankole Timothy, Carl Mutt alias Henry Ofori, and women writers (such as Regina Addae)

In other words, the paper was a bomb, and rival local newspapers saw red. It had come to show them the door to the gallows, and they weren't going to enter and come out as corpses.

Led by the Editor of one of the oldest papers, The Spectator (DR NANKA BRUCE), they tried to strangle The Graphic at birth! They petitioned the Joint Provincial Council of Chiefs (headquarters: Dodowa) not only to tell the colonial government to suppress the dangerous new paper but also to use their influence, as chiefs, to get their subjects to boycott it because it would ruin the country's traditional way of life.

The chiefs rejected the petition. But they made a proposal to the proprietors of the Graphic. They suggested that Mr Martin Therson-Cofie, Editor of the Ashanti Times (a paper owned by the Ashanti Goldfields Corporation), be approached to become Editor of the Graphic.

It looked like a good compromise--AsAshanti Goldfields was foreign-owned, but it had done nothing the chiefs had found to be subversive of their authority.

The Daily Mirror group of London, owners of the Graphic, accepted the proposal of the chiefs and Martin Therson-Cofie, a man of moderate views, became Editor of the Graphic at a time when the Gold Coast was recovering from the political shockwaves set in motion by the shooting of three Ex-servicemen by the Gold Coast police (at Osu, near the Christiansburg Castle) on 28 February 1948.

Former Finance Minister and Member of Parliament for Karaga, Dr Mohammed Amin Adam, has congratulated Professor Alhassan Musah on his appointment as Vice-Chancellor of KAAF University.

Dr Amin Adam described the appointment as a well-deserved recognition of Professor Musah’s career and contribution as an academic and development professional.

He wished the new Vice Chancellor continued success and prayed for Allah’s guidance as he takes on the leadership of KAAF University.

Ghana News.title: Mahama reaffirms commitment to Volta development at Asogli Te Za
Ghana News.content:
President John Mahama has reaffirmed his government’s commitment to the development of the Volta Region, citing youth employment, support for women entrepreneurs and regional economic collaboration as key priorities.

Dr Julius Debrah, the Chief of Staff, who represented the President as the Special Guest of Honour at the Asogli Te Za celebration, conveyed the President’s greetings to Togbe Afede XIV, traditional leaders and the people of Asogli State.

He said the President would have attended the celebration personally but was on an official trip abroad.

Dr Debrah congratulated Togbe Afede XIV on 23 years of leadership on the throne, commending his guidance and service to his people.

He wished the Agbogbomefia long life and continued strength to lead the Asogli State.

Dr Debrah also thanked the traditional ruler for his commendations of the government, saying such recognition encouraged the President and his administration to continue working for national development.

He said he would convey to President Mahama the concerns raised, including job opportunities for the youth, funding for women entrepreneurs and recommendations from a broader economic forum led by Togbe Afede XIV.

He said the government would explore ways to collaborate with traditional leadership and stakeholders to promote the overall development of the Volta Region.

Delivering the President’s message, Dr Debrah said Ghana continued to advocate fairer development, a stronger African voice in global governance, expanded trade and investment, and justice for African people.

He assured the people of the Volta Region that, although official duties might take the President beyond Ghana’s borders, the region remained close to his heart and central to the government’s development agenda.

Dr Debrah described the Asogli festival as a celebration of thanksgiving, homecoming and the renewal of bonds among the people.

He said the festival’s harvest symbolism reflected the labour of farmers, the blessings of rainfall, ancestral memory, and the promise that patient work would produce a fruitful harvest.

He praised Togbe Afede for combining traditional leadership with a forward-looking vision, saying his leadership had positioned culture as a platform for unity, enterprise and development.

Dr Debrah also commended James Gunu, the Volta Regional Minister, for his energy and practical approach to development, saying he focused on translating plans into resources and tangible outcomes for the people.

He described the people of the Volta Region as dignified, educated, industrious, and hospitable.

The address highlighted the importance of collective effort, leadership, and collaboration in advancing the region's development aspirations.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Pelosi-backed US candidate calls for ‘full arms embargo’ on Israel
World.content:
Connie Chan, endorsed by Nancy Pelosi to succeed her in California, says she will vote to ‘end a genocide in Gaza’.

Share Pelosi-backed US candidate calls for ‘full arms embargo’ on Israel on social media

Connie Chan, the US Democrat endorsed by former House of Representatives Nancy Pelosi to succeed her in California’s 11th congressional district, has called for a “full arms embargo on the Israeli government”.

In a televised debate on Thursday night, days before mail-in ballots are sent to California voters, Chan said that “on day one in Congress” she would vote to “end a genocide in Gaza and to end an apartheid state”.

Chan, a San Francisco supervisor, faces fellow Democrat and California state Senator Scott Wiener in the race to succeed Pelosi. The former House speaker, 86, is not seeking re-election.

All 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats are at stake in November’s midterm elections, with both parties vying for control of Congress.

While on Capitol Hill, Pelosi long supported Israel, condemning efforts to boycott or sanction the country and voting in favour of military aid.

Chan said humanitarian aid must be prioritised and told debate moderators she would not support funding for Israel’s Iron Dome missile defence system.

Wiener has also described Israel’s assault on Gaza as a genocide and said he would oppose funding for the Israeli military and the provision of bombs or offensive weapons.

“This government, and it’s not just [Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin] Netanyahu, is an absolute abomination, in my view, in terms of what it has inflicted on Gaza, in terms of Israel empowering settler violence and land grabs in the West Bank,” Wiener said.

The race comes amid divisions in Congress over US support for Israel. Nearly all Senate Democrats recently backed an unsuccessful effort to require a State Department report on Israel’s human rights practices, including the killings of nine Americans in the occupied West Bank.



This week, several House members also introduced the Stop the Settlements Act, which would impose sanctions on individuals and entities involved in building or expanding illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank and Gaza.

World.title: Trump ramps up pressure on US Republicans to end US clock switching
World.content:
The US president published a lawmaker’s cell phone number as he called for the passage of a bill making Daylight Saving Time permanent.

Share Trump ramps up pressure on US Republicans to end US clock switching on social media

United States President Donald Trump has increased the pressure on US Senate Republicans to make Daylight Saving Time permanent, singling out one of the body’s members for stalling legislation to end the twice-a-year changing of clocks.

In a social media post on Saturday, Trump blasted US Senator Tom Cotton for “holding up” the Sunshine Protection Act, which Trump has personally opted to call the “No More Changing of Clocks Act”.

“For some reason, Tom is stopping the Bill and, in the Senate, it’s very easy to do, it only takes one!” Trump wrote on his Truth Social account about the Arkansas Republican. “It should pass overwhelmingly, in a Bipartisan fashion”.

“Nobody wants to spend their precious time running all over the place, turning Clocks back twice a year and, having sunshine in the afternoon is better than early in the morning!” he added.

Trump went even further, publishing what he claimed was Cotton’s phone number as he implored Arkansas residents to pressure him. The move echoed a moment during the 2016 Republican presidential primaries, when then-candidate Trump gave out US Senator Lindsey Graham’s number after the former rival criticised him.

Al Jazeera called the number listed in Trump’s post, but an automated message stated the voicemail box was full. Cotton’s spokesperson and the White House did not respond to requests for comment.

The president has routinely pushed Senate Republicans to pass legislation mandating year-round daylight saving, which would end Americans’ decades-long practice of changing their clocks twice a year to increase daylight hours. On Friday, Trump urged the US Senate to approve the bill, which passed the US House in July by a 308-117 vote.



Cotton has previously opposed the bill, arguing in a US Senate floor speech last year that farmers, construction workers, commuters and children heading to school would begin their days in the dark during the winter.

Trump disputed that argument in a separate post on Saturday, saying the bill “would be a very nice and easy WIN for the Republican Party”.

“If Tom Cotton were putting Arkansas first, he would give them an extra hour of daylight and, more importantly, they wouldn’t have to run all over their houses, farms, workplaces, and everywhere else, twice a year, having to change their Clocks, and often forgetting to do so”, Trump wrote.

Trump, an avid golfer, also highlighted what he considered to be another selling point of the bill: the North American Professional Golfers’ Association (PGA) tour.

“The PGA TOUR, as an example, needs more Daylight in the afternoon in order to finish their Tournaments”, he wrote in a post, which included a letter from PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp supporting the bill. “Likewise, regular Golfers, Tennis Players, Hunters and, perhaps more importantly, Farmers who want more Daylight to play or work.”

The US president, who spent part of Saturday at his golf club in Sterling, Virginia, indicated in a subsequent post that he had received personal feedback on the proposal: “I don’t know about anyone else, but a table full of very distinguished people just told me that they HATE, immediately after a mandatory time change, going home at night – and it’s DARK. It’s depressing!”

In 1974, the US Congress briefly adopted year-round daylight saving time in response to the country’s energy crisis. But Congress repealed the law less than a year later over safety concerns as children commuted to school before sunrise.

US senators left Washington this week and have no set plans to return until after the November 3 midterm elections.

Some members, such as Senator John Kennedy, weren’t optimistic that Senate Republican Leader John Thune would bring the bill up for a vote before polling day.

“It’s dead as disco,” the Louisiana Republican told Reuters this week of Trump’s push to make daylight saving time permanent. “My sense is it would have trouble passing … I don’t think the leader is going to bring it up.”

World.title: Remains of Bulgaria’s Czar Samuel return ‘home’ after 1,000 years
World.content:
The emperor is a symbol of Bulgarian national identity whose repatriation stoked tensions with Greece.

More than 1,000 years after his death, the remains of medieval ruler Czar Samuel have arrived in Bulgaria.

A symbol of Bulgarian national identity, Samuel was a warrior emperor who battled the Byzantine Empire to expand his kingdom before suffering defeat and dying soon after in 1014. His supposed remains were discovered in a Greek border area in the 1960s.

The coffin and remains were flown on Saturday to the Bulgarian capital, Sofia, on board a military aircraft that was surrounded by air force fighter jets.

Thousands of people poured into a public square to honour the czar’s arrival, which capped years of fraught negotiations between Bulgaria and Greece until an accord was reached this week.

Bulgarian politicians across the spectrum paid tribute to the medieval ruler, listening to the national anthem and a 21-gun salute.

“Today, we Europeans are learning to read history with a desire to belong not only to our homeland, but also to the culture that unites us across the entire European continent,” Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said.

“That is why Europe must not reopen old wounds but must work for peace as the supreme good,” Radev continued, referring to the centuries-old rivalry between neighbouring Greece and Bulgaria.

Crowds cheered as fighter jets performed a flypast.

Martin Nestorov, a 42-year-old software engineer, told the AFP news agency he attended the ceremony “to welcome Czar Samuel back to Bulgaria, where he belongs”.

“I am here because I am Bulgarian, and a Bulgarian is returning to his homeland,” added Tsanka Zlatkova, 65, a retired art historian.



A procession brought the remains to be laid in the Church of Saint Sofia, a sixth-century basilica that is the capital’s namesake and where church officials say Samuel was baptised.

Competing claims

The handover of Samuel’s remains is part of a broader accord between the Greek and Bulgarian culture ministers.

In exchange, Greece is slated to receive 48 objects that Bulgarian troops pillaged from churches and monasteries in Greece during World War I.

Speaking before the handover, Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said he hoped the ceremony would boost Greece’s campaign to repatriate the Parthenon Marbles, a collection of 2,500-year-old marble sculptures taken from the Acropolis in Athens and later displayed in the British Museum.

“The global community is essentially re-evaluating its longstanding stance on protecting cultural heritage,” Mitsotakis said, adding that historical heirlooms “cannot be treated as the spoils of war”.

Bulgaria is not the only country to have claims on Samuel. A huge statue of the czar stands in the North Macedonian capital of Skopje, with Macedonians claiming him as “their” ruler.

In 2022, a bilateral commission recommended presenting Samuel as the head of a state that “most contemporary historiographers consider to be the Bulgarian Empire”, based in what is currently North Macedonia.
