World.title: Biljana Plavsic, Bosnian Serb War Criminal Who Withdrew Her Remorse
World.content:
The Serb political elites do not recognise the legitimacy of the ICTY and believe, as Plavsic did, that the court was set up “to prosecute Serbs”. Lack of recognition of the court as a legitimate, bipartisan institution has led to many high-ranking war criminals returning to Serbia and being welcomed as heroes, and/or buried with the highest state honours.

Plavsic never changed her convictions. In her now infamous statement of guilt at the ICTY, she apologised for the persecution of “thousands of non-Serbs” during her sentencing hearing in 2002. “I have now come to the belief and accept the fact that many thousands of innocent people were the victims of an organised, systematic effort to remove Muslims and Croats from the territory claimed by Serbs,” she said.

“Although I was repeatedly informed of allegations of cruel and inhuman conduct against non-Serbs, I refused to accept them or even to investigate. The knowledge that I am responsible for such human suffering and for soiling the character of my people will always be with me,” she added.

But, two years later, in an interview from her prison cell in Sweden, Plavsic withdrew her expression of remorse, saying she had done “nothing wrong”. Her denial of any responsibility for the crimes she was convicted of was met with outrage on behalf of victims’ organisations and the international community.

Although Plavsic may be buried with honours in Republika Srpska, she remains a controversial figure among some Serbs because she was the only high-ranking Serb leader who expressed remorse. Some have not forgiven her for this move.

“She should have never apologised and admitted that Serbs committed crimes,” I was told by some of Plavsic’s close acquaintances during my research. I think the backlash Plavsic received from Serbs after her infamous statement of guilt made her adamant in denying it and ultimately withdrawing her remorse. My impression was that she had a strong urge to go down in history as unrepentant.

To regain the image she had lost because of her unpopular expression of remorse, she repeatedly insisted that she did not regret anything she was accused of. On the contrary, she told me on many occasions, “I would do the same again. I had to protect my people. If I contributed anything in establishing Republika Srpska, our Serb state, and I know I did, there is nothing to regret.”

But although she has been called one of the “founders of Republika Srpska”, Plavsic is no longer a household name for the post-war generations of Serbs like her compatriots Ratko Mladic and Radovan Karadzic – who never apologised for their crimes.

Olivera Simic is a professor at Griffith Law School, Griffith University, Australia. She is the author of the book ‘Madam War Criminal: Biljana Plavsic, Serbia’s Iron Lady’, published by Hurst, 2025.

The opinions expressed are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the views of BIRN.

World.title: Week in Review: Elections and Struggles
World.content:
As Bosnia and Herzegovina heads to the polls, promises of political renewal are colliding with entrenched habits that cut across party lines. The governing Trojka [Trio] has struggled to deliver the clean break from clientelism and politicised institutions it promised, potentially opening a path back to power for the unreformed main Bosniak party, the Party of Democratic Action, SDA – less through renewed enthusiasm for the party than from voter disappointment and apathy.

Women’s participation in politics is another key issue. Although women account for more than 40 per cent of candidates as a result of legal obligations, they head just 15.5 per cent of the electoral lists, with parties often placing them low down, where their chances of winning are slim.

More than a decade later, Dzeko was part of the team that secured Bosnia and Herzegovina’s second World Cup qualification, earning a place at the 2026 tournament. He reached his 150th international appearance during the group stage.

World.title: Police From Three Continents Test Anti-Riot Tactics in Romania
World.content:
More than 500 riot police and gendarmerie personnel from 19 countries gathered at the Romanian Gendarmerie’s training centre in Ochiuri this week to act out security-crisis scenarios in which they tested tactics to quell angry rioters throwing projectiles, setting up barricades and attacking public buildings.

The Carpathian Blue Shield 2026 exercise was designed to test joint responses to complex security situations, including coordination, information-sharing and tactical intervention. Participants included forces from Ukraine, Moldova, Bulgaria and the US as well as Western European countries.

Romanian Interior Minister Catalin Predoiu said security risks “are becoming increasingly interconnected”, which requires public-order forces to adapt and train for real-world scenarios involving multiple threats.

World.title: Polish Activists Open the World’s First Parcel-Locker Machine for Abortion Pills
World.content:
Women Help Women, an international abortion-support network, this week unveiled the Abortomat, which it describes as the world’s first parcel-locker machine for abortion pills. It stands inside AboTak, an abortion-support clinic that opened opposite the Polish parliament in the spring of 2025.

The idea behind it is simple: make getting abortion pills closer to picking up an ordinary delivery. Poland has one of Europe’s densest networks of automated parcel lockers. More than 66,700 machines were operating across the country by the end of 2025 – roughly one for every 560 people – collecting clothes, books, groceries and whatever else people order online.

“Parcel lockers are everywhere in Poland – people joke about our ‘paczkoza’, our obsession with them,” Kinga Jelinska, director of Women Help Women, told BIRN. “So why not use that same technology for abortion pills, where getting them to someone faster can actually matter?”

The process involves a person contacting Women Help Women online and, after a consultation, receiving a six-digit code. That code opens one of 22 compartments containing the medication. The machine was designed by engineers and IT specialists commissioned by the organisation and, unlike commercial parcel lockers, does not store users’ personal data, Jelinska explained.

“Sometimes even waiting a few days can be too long,” she said. “For people whose health is at risk, or who are further along in pregnancy, every day really matters.”

In Poland, that wait exists partly because abortion care remains caught between a restrictive legal system and an extensive informal network built to work around it. Abortion is legal only when a pregnancy threatens a woman’s life or health, or results from a criminal act. Helping someone obtain an abortion outside those circumstances can be punishable by up to three years in prison under Article 152 of the criminal code. The pregnant person however is not criminally liable for ending their own pregnancy.

Donald Tusk’s governing coalition came to power in 2023 promising to change the law, but reform has repeatedly stalled. A bill partially decriminalising assistance in abortion has remained in a special parliamentary committee since 2024. In the meantime, activists have filled much of the gap. Abortion Without Borders, a network of Polish and international groups, says it supported 38,508 abortions in 2025, making it the largest de facto abortion care provider in Poland.

The Abortomat pushes that parallel system one step further – and tests the legal boundary surrounding it. “The person collecting the pills is not committing a crime, and the machine itself cannot be prosecuted,” Justyna Wydrzynska of Abortion Dream Team, the collective that runs the Warsaw clinic, said at the launch.

Wydrzynska has personal experience of that boundary. In 2023, she was convicted of assisting an abortion after sending pills to a woman who had sought help during the Covid pandemic. An appeals court later overturned the conviction and ordered a retrial.

Some lawyers are unconvinced that putting a machine between the activist and the person taking the pills changes much. “Assistance can cover a very broad range of actions,” criminal lawyer Pawel Matyja told Polish news outlet Zero.pl, arguing that sending the medication, arranging its collection and providing the access code could together still amount to assisting an abortion. “These are essentially a series of steps without which the woman would not be able to have the abortion.”

For the time being, the Abortomat will remain indoors for security reasons, Jelinska said. She would much rather put it outside, but since AboTak opened, anti-abortion protesters have regularly gathered outside its entrance. Some demonstrations have involved loudspeakers and vuvuzelas, while the premises have also been targeted with butyric acid.

“Our aim is to draw attention to an institution operating in the heart of the capital which, in our view, violates Polish law. We will continue protesting until it is closed,” Laura Lipinska of the Zycie i Rodzina Foundation, which participates in the protests, said in a statement after the centre opened in 2025.

Despite the protests and legal uncertainty, the activists are pressing ahead. “If we worried about what might happen, or how people might react,” Jelinska said, “we wouldn’t have done anything for the past 12 years.”

World.title: After Bosnia’s ‘Anaemic’ Election Campaign, Polling Day Sees New Challenge
World.content:
On Saturday, the day before Bosnians vote in general elections, election officials in some 5,700 polling stations are due to switch on scanners and fingerprint readers that most of the country has never used before. This is to run tests and so determine whether the technology works properly.

“It is a logistical challenge,” Tihana Bartulec Blanc, president of the US-based NGO Civic Hub and a veteran international election observer, told BIRN.

BIRN spoke to three experts about the impact of the nationwide debut of biometric voter checks and ballot scanners, which arrives in a campaign that analysts otherwise describe as lacklustre.

World.title: Democracy Digest: Operation Purgatory Snares Former Hungarian Ministers
World.content:
Fico juggles jobs and coalition; another fatal school attack shocks Slovakia

Robert Fico is currently Slovakia’s prime minister and, temporarily, its environment minister. The second job may prove easier than keeping his three-party coalition together. On Wednesday, President Peter Pellegrini handed the environment portfolio to Fico after dismissing Tomas Taraba. Taraba’s increasingly bitter feud with Slovak National Party (SNS) leader Andrej Danko culminated in an unprecedented episode in Slovakia’s recent political history: SNS MPs joining the opposition in voting to remove a minister nominated by their own party, after Fico had rejected a request to dismiss Taraba. The minister’s exit resolves one problem but leaves Fico with a larger one. Back in parliament as an independent MP, Taraba says he remains loyal to Fico, but will decide on how to vote on a case-by-case basis. With 76 votes needed for a majority, the government has little room for such conditional loyalty – particularly with the 2027 budget due in October. If parliament fails to approve it, Slovakia would enter a provisional budget regime, limiting monthly spending to one-twelfth of the current year’s budget. The coalition reckons it has 78 MPs, but that number could fall on individual votes. There is no obvious replacement for Taraba either. SNS claims the Environment Ministry under the coalition agreement and wants Deputy Environment Minister Filip Kuffa, though Taraba himself has questioned Kuffa’s qualifications. Kuffa has also faced criticism from the opposition in the past. The turmoil revived speculation about an early election, an option Fico himself recently put on the table. For now, however, the three coalition parties have strong reasons to keep the government alive. SNS is polling below the threshold for entering parliament, while coalition partner Hlas opposes an early vote, saying it has yet to deliver everything it promised its voters. Fico also has major projects and unfinished legislative business he may want to see through. Moreover, ending parliament’s term requires 90 MPs, meaning the coalition would also need opposition votes. At this point, an early election remains possible, though not probable. Fico and his Smer party have survived bigger challenges in the past, most notably in 2018 after the murder of investigative journalist Jan Kuciak and his fiancee, Martina Kusnirova, and subsequent mass protests. Fico resigned as prime minister, but Smer remained in government until the 2020 election.

Slovakia is again confronting violence in its schools this week after a 13-year-old boy killed a teacher and a classmate in the northern village of Staskov, northern Slovakia. Bozena Mariakova, 61, and the unnamed female pupil died after the boy attacked them with a knife. He also seriously wounded another teacher, whose condition is now reported as being stable. The boy has been placed in a psychological detention facility. At 13, he cannot be held criminally responsible under Slovak law. What happened before the attack is now under scrutiny. Days earlier, the murdered girl had reportedly alerted teachers to an image created by the boy showing a concentration camp with teachers’ faces. He could have had his conduct grade lowered over the incident. Psychologists spent two hours with his class on Monday, while the school had also filed a criminal complaint with police five days before the attack. Police are now reviewing how local officers dealt with that complaint. Little is publicly known about the boy. Residents told Slovak media he was being raised by his grandmother and mentioned unspecified difficulties involving his mother. A woman who knew him from church remembered him as a bright boy who served at Mass and read well, but rarely appeared cheerful. The attack comes less than two years after a student killed two people at a school in Spisska Stara Ves, eastern Slovakia. It also coincides with parliament debating a government bill on preventing radicalisation and mobilisation to violence among young people.

World.title: Construction begins on first phase of Iraq’s Madinat Al Ward
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – ORA Iraq awarded CRC Dorra the building contract for the first phase of Madinat Al Ward, paving the way for large-scale development in Iraq.

The deal was signed in the presence of Naguib Sawiris, Chairman of ORA, and Mohamed Dorra, Vice Chairman of Dorra Group, as the project progressed from ground preparation to primary construction.

CRC Dorra will begin construction after POWERCHINA has completed the earthworks and ground preparation for Phase One, according to ORA Iraq.

The deal adds another important regional contractor to the development.

CRC Dorra is the contracting arm of Dorra Group, an engineering and construction business founded in 1943 that operates in Egypt, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and Iraq.

Its work includes residential, commercial, office, and hotel developments, as well as design-build projects.

ORA said that the selection was based on CRC Dorra’s construction expertise and capacity to perform large-scale projects.

The commencement of construction marks a key milestone for Madinat Al Ward as ORA expands its investment and development efforts in the Iraqi market.

The company said that it continues to be dedicated to building the project as an integrated community, with the new contract advancing Phase One from site preparation to physical construction.

World.title: US Treasury approves waiver for Iranian flights to Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Foreign Affairs Fuad Hussein announced on Friday, October 2, 2026, that U.S. Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent has agreed to exempt religious pilgrimage flights to holy sites in Iraq from secondary sanctions imposed on Iranian aviation, following intensive bilateral talks held in Washington.

The decision resolves mounting diplomatic friction surrounding the status of Najaf International Airport, granting legal clarity for passenger arrivals while shielding Iraqi aviation infrastructure from punitive measures.

In a statement shared on X (formerly Twitter) and reported by the 964 Network, Hussein outlined that discussions with Bessent encompassed the overarching trajectory of U.S.-Iraqi economic and security ties, regional fiscal stability, and the spillover impacts of American sanctions enforcement on the domestic Iraqi economy.

Hussein specifically raised the operational paralysis facing Najaf International Airport—a vital national transport hub serving millions of international religious pilgrims annually—emphasizing that economic restrictions should not impede lawful civilian travel or religious observances. Secretary Bessent acknowledged Iraq’s sovereign concerns, formally approving a targeted waiver for flights directed toward the holy shrines.

During the diplomatic session, Hussein reaffirmed Baghdad’s appreciation for past U.S. and International Coalition support in the campaign to defeat Daesh (ISIS), while reiterating the federal government’s constitutional roadmap under Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi to monopolize arms under the state and maintain sole authority over war and peace.

Commending Washington’s accommodation, Hussein noted that recognizing the importance of religious freedom and facilitating pilgrim transit reflects shared values of mutual respect and tolerance, reinforcing a stable, long-term bilateral partnership between Iraq and the United States.

World.title: ITEX 2026: Iraqi AI and tech startups expand
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi, regional, and international technology enterprises showcased cutting-edge solutions in artificial intelligence, network synchronization, and enterprise digital transformation during their participation in the Iraq International Information and Communications Technology Exhibition in Baghdad.

The participating companies expressed strong ambition to expand operations and capture growing commercial opportunities in Iraq’s rapidly developing technological sector.

Hassan Abdul-Baqi Khalaf, founder of domestic startup Al-Burhan for AI Image and Video Recognition, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the venture originated from registered patents specializing in automated media verification and tamper protection against digital forgery and deepfakes.

Khalaf—a computer science student at the American University of Iraq – Baghdad (AUIB) collaborating with a doctoral partner in mathematics and physics—highlighted that their platform processes requests for more than 3,000 daily active users across private corporate clients and the public.

Delivering up to 95 percent accuracy in identifying manipulated content, the company is leveraging its inaugural exhibition presence to pursue operational partnerships with federal entities, specifically the Ministry of Interior, to detect fabricated media and enhance sovereign cyber verification tools.

International infrastructure providers also underscored their entry into the domestic market. Engineer Ahmed Mustafa of Canada’s Al-Mamas, an IT and network engineering specialist, revealed that the firm is seeking to establish an operational foothold in Iraq following successful deployments in the UAE, Qatar, and Egypt.

Al-Mamas holds exclusive distribution rights across the Middle East and North Africa for precision German-manufactured timing and synchronization hardware, which is critical for maintaining ultra-low-latency architectures across telecommunications networks, industrial automation, data center facilities, and distributed artificial intelligence systems.

Highlighting regional corporate expansion, Samer Al-Yasin, sales director for Qatar-headquartered conglomerate Mannai Corporation, affirmed that Iraq represents a fertile and attractive destination for long-term tech investment.

Marking its second exhibition appearance in Baghdad, Mannai—which employs over 15,000 personnel across the Gulf—formally established its Baghdad branch three months ago and is actively preparing to launch regional offices in Erbil and Basra.

Al-Yasin emphasized that the group is deploying enterprise digital transformation, cloud integration, and systems architecture tailored for federal ministries, banking institutions, and healthcare providers, aiming to transfer its regional technical expertise to drive national modernization and support sovereign institutional revenues.

World.title: Baghdad hosts major motorsports festival to celebrate Iraqi sovereignty day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Baghdad hosted a mass motorsports festival on Friday, October 2, 2026, to celebrate Iraqi Sovereignty Day and National Day, organized under the auspices of Iraqi National Olympic Committee President Aqeel Muften and drawing substantial public crowds alongside national sports figures.

The festival, co-organized by the Iraqi Automobile and Motorcycle Federation and secured by the Baghdad Operations Command, showcased competitive and exhibition motorsport performances to highlight domestic stability and nationwide celebrations marking the complete withdrawal of foreign forces.

Farooq Al-Rubaie, President of the Iraqi Automobile and Motorcycle Federation, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that celebrating Sovereignty Day honors the resilience and immense sacrifices made by the armed forces and citizens over challenging decades.

Noting the passionate grassroots fanbase for motorsports across Iraq, Al-Rubaie emphasized that staging the festival serves both an athletic and patriotic duty, projecting the reality of a secure and revitalized capital. He urged local and regional media outlets along with content creators to spotlight Iraq’s stability, community engagements, and peaceful public life during major national milestones.

Baghdad Operations Command Media Director, Major General Abbas Hamid, stated to INA that Sovereignty Day—coinciding with Iraq’s National Day—reflects the sovereign resolve of the Iraqi people.

Hamid confirmed that joint security formations under the Ministries of Defense and Interior, alongside military intelligence branches, established comprehensive security perimeters around the capital to safeguard wide-ranging cultural, artistic, and athletic gatherings.

Reaffirming that Baghdad is entering an era defined by urban reconstruction and civic stability, Hamid reiterated the full readiness of security apparatuses to protect public safety and preserve social cohesion across all urban centers.

World.title: Iraq inks data center MoU with Huawei as tech giant employs 10,000 across country
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Communications formalized a strategic partnership with global telecommunications giant Huawei on Friday, October 2, 2026, signing a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to construct modern enterprise data centers across the country.

Finalized during the 5th Iraq International Information and Communications Technology Exhibition and Conference (ITEX 2026) in Baghdad, the agreement was concluded under the sponsorship and in the presence of Minister of Communications Mustafa Sanad between the state-owned General Company for Communications and Informatics and Huawei’s executive leadership.

The initiative is aimed at bolstering Iraq’s sovereign cloud hosting, elevating service quality, and broadening international technical cooperation.

On the sidelines of the expo, Huawei confirmed the extensive scope of its commercial footprint in Iraq, revealing that it actively partners with more than 240 domestic Iraqi enterprises across diverse sectors.

Rafid Abbas Al-Khafaji, Vice President and Board Member of Huawei Iraq, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that this marked the company’s inaugural participation as an exhibitor at ITEX, expressing admiration for the high caliber of domestic and multinational engagement.

Al-Khafaji noted that Huawei presented specialized end-to-end solutions spanning oil and gas digitalization, telecommunications, smart transportation, healthcare systems, artificial intelligence, and modular data center architecture.

Reviewing the company’s continuous commercial presence in Iraq since 2003, Al-Khafaji emphasized that Huawei remained fully operational through all domestic security and economic challenges, including uninterrupted on-site work by its Chinese engineering teams during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Today, the corporation operates four major regional branches in Baghdad, Basra, Erbil, and Sulaymaniyah, supporting a wider ecosystem of over 10,000 employees.

Addressing public misconceptions, Al-Khafaji clarified that while Huawei is widely recognized among consumers for consumer smartphones, handset sales represent the smallest segment of its business portfolio by volume.

The firm’s enterprise and carrier operations form the backbone of its Iraqi footprint, servicing major mobile network operators alongside key sovereign institutions, including the Ministries of Oil, Transport, Interior, and Defense, as well as the General Secretariat of the Council of Ministers.

Beyond central government networks, Huawei is driving provincial smart security solutions—such as Babylon Governorate’s integrated municipal surveillance network—while advancing intelligent electric vehicle systems and cloud infrastructures designed to anchor Iraq’s next-generation digital economy.

World.title: Russia ‘tearing Kyiv apart’, mayor says, as strikes paralyse traffic
World.content:
Kyiv – Russian attacks on key infrastructure were “tearing Kyiv apart”, the city’s mayor said Friday, as strikes on a bridge linking the capital’s east and west brought traffic to a standstill.

President Volodymyr Zelensky accused his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, of ripping up the rulebook of armed conflict by sanctioning massive attacks on civilian areas, an accusation the Kremlin has rejected.

The grinding conflict, which began with Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, has largely focused on ground fighting in the east, with Kyiv largely spared from the devastation wrought near the frontline.

But Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said the city should now be on a war footing.

“The capital is in a very dramatic situation,” he posted on Telegram. “It’s no longer possible to pretend that we can live now as we lived in peacetime.

“The enemy is tearing Kyiv apart.”

His message came as the authorities shut one of Kyiv’s main bridges and restricted movement on a second after another wave of deadly strikes by fast-moving, jet-powered drones.

Long lines of stationary cars and buses were gridlocked on main roads as commuters sought alternative routes — or even made their way on foot.

“I’ve been travelling for three hours… to get to work,” said Tetiana Osypenko, a 49-year-old seamstress whose bus was stuck in a traffic jam.

“There’s just no way to get there. Nothing. It’s impossible to cross the bridges today,” she told AFP.

Traffic built up due to the complete closure to all vehicles going in both directions on the Southern Bridge, one of eight bridges connecting the east and west of Kyiv over the Dnipro river.

It was hit several times on Thursday and Friday morning.

The Paton Bridge, further north, was open in one direction only, though there were no reports that it had been struck.

In a post on X, Zelensky accused Putin of last month declaring there were “no rules now”, citing unnamed intelligence and people around Putin.

“The Russians couldn’t occupy us. So now they are doing massive attacks and massive killings,” Zelensky said.

The Kremlin made no immediate public response to the claim, which Zelensky first made in an interview with the Financial Times.

– Daily disruption –

Kyiv has been increasingly under aerial bombardment in recent months, putting the city on near-constant alert and disrupting daily life.

Air raid sirens warning of approaching threats in the skies sound almost round the clock, urging the city’s estimated three million people to seek shelter.

Repeated strikes on trains and petrol stations have already hit the rail and road networks while attacks on energy facilities threaten power and heating as winter approaches.

Osypenko, the seamstress, said she would not get home because of the traffic jams. Previous disruption to subway services during air raids forced her to spend the night in a metro station near the Southern Bridge.

Not being able to work costs her money, compounding the financial pressures caused by the war, she added. “You just spend the whole day feeling completely beaten down.”

The latest Russian attacks killed one person and wounded at least two other people when a 25-storey residential building was hit in southeast Kyiv.

– ‘Political will’ –

Zelensky urged tougher sanctions to prevent Russia from manufacturing its new jet-powered drones, which are faster and harder to intercept.

Russia’s production of the weapons was “critically dependent” on foreign components, he wrote on social media on Friday.

“Every Russian drone can actually be stopped right at the production line. What is needed is the political will of these countries,” he added.

Zelensky has repeatedly called on Ukraine’s Western allies for more military support, particularly for US-made Patriot missile interceptors.

On Thursday, he said Ukraine had used its FP-7 tactical ballistic missile in combat for the first time, without disclosing where or what it had been used against.

He also said Ukraine was testing five of its own interceptors against drones.

Ukraine’s military on Friday said it struck an oil refinery in Volgograd and another facility in Samara, both in southwest Russia, for allegedly supplying fuel to Russian forces.

Kyiv also dismissed reports that its F-16 fighter jets — another key tool used against jet-powered drones — could be grounded due to delays in maintenance inspection and the supply of parts.

But Zelensky told the Financial Times that around half of Ukraine’s fleet was spending lengthy maintenance periods in Europe.

World.title: Man City verdict a ‘big topic’ for England players, says Tuchel
World.content:
London – Thomas Tuchel said that Manchester City were the talk of the England camp after the club were found guilty of multiple breaches of Premier League financial rules, but insisted that the case would not affect his selection for Saturday’s match in Croatia.

The findings by an independent commission, announced earlier this week, have sent shockwaves through English football.

City, the dominant Premier League force over the past 15 years, face severe sanctions, which could include expulsion from the top division.

Marc Guehi and Elliott Anderson are the only two City players remaining in Tuchel’s squad for the Nations League match in Rijeka after Nico O’Reilly was forced to withdraw due to injury.

“We had some time off and some time between the matches, and it’s a big subject,” Tuchel told his pre-match press conference on Friday.

“Of course the players talk about it, and City players talk about it, and we talk to them, but only briefly.

“They’re ready to go for tomorrow, that’s what they show on the pitch and that’s what they show in camp, but of course it’s a big topic.”

City deny wrongdoing and on Friday lodged an appeal against the ruling.

But unless they can overturn the decision of the commission, they are likely to face at least a points deduction, which would threaten their place in the Premier League.

Tuchel was asked if the club’s players would still be in his mind for selection should they be playing regularly in the lower divisions.

“There’s always a possibility,” he said. “I think I would always try to pick the best team for the camp, for the occasion, for the tournament, and I will never rule out that they don’t play in the top flight in their country.

“So we need to look at this from case by case.”

England’s clash with Croatia, which will take place behind closed doors, is their third of four Nations League games in the current international window.

The Three Lions were beaten 3-2 by world champions Spain on home soil last weekend, but bounced back to beat the Czech Republic 2-0 on Tuesday.

World.title: US posts weak job growth data in September
World.content:
Washington – Employment in the United States grew by 29,000 jobs in September, missing analysts’ expectations significantly, with the unemployment rate rising slightly to 4.2 percent, government data showed on Friday.

Adding to the weak data, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) also revised down job figures for July and August by a combined 60,000 jobs, the department said in a statement.

The revision to July’s data showed that the world’s largest economy lost jobs that month, as opposed to posting a gain of 21,000 as previously reported.

The data comes ahead of key midterm elections in November where President Donald Trump’s Republican Party is facing a stern test over his handling of the economy.

Analysts polled by Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal had expected the US economy to add 84,000 jobs in September.

– Health care leads –

Employment in most major sectors was largely unchanged, the BLS reported, with health care posting notable gains of 17,000.

The sector has propped up the labor market in the United States in the last year, as an aging population requires more care both in hospitals and at home.

Still, September’s gains in the sector were slower than its average monthly gain of 33,000 over the last year.

The financial sector continued its downward slide, losing 7,000 jobs in September and bringing its overall slump from a recent peak in May 2025 to 129,000.

Most of the losses in that sector have been among insurance companies.

– Fed implications –

Average hourly earnings for all employees were up 3.0 percent, the BLS said, with wages continuing to lag behind stubbornly high inflation — meaning most workers are seeing real wage losses.

Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren seized on the data to criticize Trump’s performance since taking office last year.

“Paychecks are growing at their slowest rate in nearly seven years, outside of the Covid-19 pandemic,” she said in a statement.

“Since the start of Trump’s war, real wages have fallen 0.7 percent as his failed agenda keeps pushing prices up,” she said, referring to the US war against Iran launched in late February.

The conflict has plunged the Middle East into violence and sent global energy prices skyrocketing, as Tehran’s retaliatory action has targeted Washington’s regional allies and choked a key trading route.

The data comes after the US Federal Reserve — which has a dual mandate to maintain inflation at a long-term two-percent target while ensuring maximum employment — raised interest rates last month to address high prices.

The US labor market has been largely in balance this year, with modest job gains and a relatively steady unemployment rate.

That steadiness has allowed the Fed to focus on the inflation side of its mandate, but any weakness in the labor market may give policy makers pause.

Raising interest rates tends to cool inflation but can also limit economic activity, which can affect the job market.

This week, two key Fed policymakers indicated that the central bank may not raise rates again at its October meeting, although markets continue to expect a further hike before the end of the year.

Friday’s jobs data “lends support to the less hawkish Fed officials that indicate no need to rush and deliver the next rate hike at the end of this month,” said Kathy Bostjancic, chief economist at Nationwide, in a note.

She added that this could release some pressure on bond yields — which have been spiralling in part due to expectations of interest rate hikes.

Nancy Vanden Houten at Oxford Economics, however, disagreed, expecting upside risks to inflation to continue to dominate Fed policymakers’ thinking.

“We think the upside risks to inflation are still a bigger concern for the Federal Reserve and expect they will raise rates at the end of the month,” she said.

World.title: Insurance companies want policyholders to pay 10% of health claims
World.content:
The proposal, being considered by the General Insurance Council, would pair the change with common hospital empanelment and a formal mechanism for settling disputes between insurers and hospitals.

Outpatient claims would remain outside scheme

MUMBAI: Non-life insurers are considering a 10% co-payment by policyholders on retail health policies from Jan 1, 2027, with the patient's contribution capped at Rs 5 lakh per claim. In return, customers would pay lower annual premiums.The proposal, being considered by the General Insurance Council, would pair the change with common hospital empanelment and a formal mechanism for settling disputes between insurers and hospitals. The arrangement would require even those with comprehensive health insurance to keep funds for medical emergencies, as they would have to pay 10% of admissible inpatient hospitalisation costs, including those arising from accidents, whether claims are settled through cashless procedure or reimbursement.The proposal covers retail indemnity products, retail-under-group policies, indemnity components of combi products, internal migrations and portability business. Outpatient claims would remain outside the scheme.Co-payment cannot be waived, reduced or modified through riders or endorsements, and the customerâs 10% contribution cannot be recovered from another health insurance policy.âThe choice between a cheaper policy with a deductible and a full-compensation policy should rest with the insured.People buy insurance to be indemnified for their costs. It would be unfair to customers willing to pay a higher premium for a higher sum insured to still bear part of the cost, and this could discourage them from buying high-value policies,â said Shreeraj Deshpande, a health insurance expert who earlier headed operations at a general insurer. While the industry is seeking to address what it sees as cost distortions in healthcare, some fear a mandatory requirement could be anti-competitive. âIf the industry collectively decides that no one will offer a full-compensation policy, it might catch the attention of the Competition Commission,â said an industry executive.The logic behind the measure is that hospitals may order additional diagnostic tests, recommend procedures and extend hospital stays when patients have comprehensive insurance cover. Higher-category rooms can also increase total bills because doctorsâ fees and procedure charges are often linked to room tariffs.With insurance covering the full bill, patients may have less incentive to question charges or choose lower-cost hospitals.âThis behaviour (overbilling and provider-induced demand) stems from the perception that insurance-backed patients are less price-sensitive, leading to inflated healthcare costs,â a council note said.The proposal also calls for common hospital empanelment, outcome-based contracts and a payor-provider grievance forum. GI Council plans standard empanelment across more than 4,300 hospitals to set benchmark tariffs and curb arbitrary billing, while linking contracts to clinical and procedure-wise outcomes.

World.title: PK Mishra: India must stay open, but not become vulnerable
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India needs to remain open to the world without becoming âexcessively vulnerableâ to the globe amid export restrictions, sanctions and tariffs being weaponised, principal secretary to PM PK Mishra said on Saturday.

At the Kautilya Economic Conclave, Mishra said the changing nature of trade policy was adding to uncertainty for economies. âThe question before policymakers is not whether globalisation has ended... The question is how we preserve the gains from openness while making economies less vulnerable to concentrated and unpredictable shocks.â The economic logic of globalisation was built around specialisation and production where costs are lowest, and goods move efficiently across borders.

World.title: Rs 3,750 crore RCom fraud: CBI names ex-LIC executive
World.content:
According to CBI, its investigation revealed that in 2012, LIC subscribed to Non-Convertible Debentures worth Rs 1,500 crore issued by Reliance Communications Ltd. based on serious misrepresentations.

NEW DELHI: CBI has filed a chargesheet against Reliance Communications Ltd and three key executives in a Rs 3,750 crore fraud case alleged by Life Insurance Corporation (LIC). The document names Amitabh Jhunjhunwala, Group MD of Reliance ADA Group, Vishwas Joshi, senior VP of Reliance Capital Limited, and P Venugopal, the then chief investment officer of LIC. CBI filed its report before the special judge for CBI cases in Mumbai.The accused have been charged with offences of criminal conspiracy, cheating, and criminal breach of trust under IPC sections, alongside charges under the Prevention of Corruption Act.According to CBI, its investigation revealed that in 2012, LIC subscribed to Non-Convertible Debentures worth Rs 1,500 crore issued by Reliance Communications Ltd. based on serious misrepresentations."The funds received from the subscription were subsequently diverted to other Reliance ADA Group companies, resulting in wrongful gain to the accused while causing a total alleged loss of â¹3,750 crore to LIC," CBI has said in the chargesheet.The probe agency had registered this case on April 1, 2026, following a complaint lodged by LIC. This submission represents the eighth chargesheet filed by the agency in a broader crackdown on Reliance ADA Group entities.CBI has registered nine FIRs against Reliance Communications Limited, Reliance Home Finance Limited and other group entities. These FIRs stem from complaints by various public sector banks, LIC and Employees' Provident Fund Organisation. Seven have been arrested in these cases.

World.title: Finance system resilient, economy braved West Asia crisis: RBI governor
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

Sanjay Malhotra on Saturday said the Indian financial system remained resilient and the economy had navigated the West Asia crisis well, but policymakers needed to stay vigilant.

"We cannot afford to become complacent; the economic and financial costs of allowing vulnerabilities to build up are simply too high... Today's resilience may not necessarily imply tomorrow's immunity. We are committed to remaining vigilant of emerging vulnerabilities and continuing to keep our financial system strong and resilient," he said at the Kautilya Economic Conclave, organised by the Institute of Economic Growth and the finance ministry.

He cautioned against the possible adverse impact of the war in Iran, which has hit supply chains. "The financial system has absorbed the supply shock due to the West Asia conflict well. However, the global economic environment remains challenging. The conflict has exacerbated inflationary pressures and enhanced financial system vulnerabilities," the RBI governor said, adding India was navigating from a position of strength.





Malhotra cautioned against stressed valuations, especially those related to AI, elevated debt levels globally, elevated leverage that could spill over to banks and markets in case of tightening of financial conditions, private credit, and cyber risks that have been compounded by AI.

"Strong macroeconomic fundamentals and a resilient financial system provide confidence in our ability to withstand this lingering shock.

At the same time, we are taking further measures to enhance our resilience to such shocks," he said, listing diversification of import sources, greater self-sufficiency in energy and other critical resources, enhancing manufacturing competitiveness, expanding market access through free trade agreements, and promoting trade settlement in local currencies, among others.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The RBI governor also said Indian bond yields had risen only partially in response to higher global energy prices and global yields, reflecting the prudence in fiscal management, credible monetary policy and declining structural pressure on inflation.

He said the Indian private credit market remained small, equity markets had corrected in recent months, and cyber risk governance had been strengthened. "Overall, the financial system is assessed to be very resilient, supported by healthy balance sheets of banks and NBFIs," Malhotra said.

World.title: Resource security key as global economy faces uncertainty: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union finance minister

on Saturday said that amid uncertainty, ânow a standing conditionâ of the global economy, national security requires structural autonomy in strategic inputs, as strategic resource security sits at the centre of macroeconomic policy.

Besides, she argued for private investment to lead the cycle, including in research and innovation and skilling to prepare people for a changing world of work, while asserting that global financial architecture should reflect where growth was coming from.

âWe need to keep building resilience as we go along; itâs not a one-time exercise. The coming years call for preparation, and India approaches them from strength,â she said at Kautilya Economic Conclave.

The remarks assume significance amid global economic uncertainties triggered by US tariffs and conflicts in Ukraine and West Asia, which have disrupted global supply chains and resulted in higher prices of key commodities.

âA price shock can be cushioned with monetary and fiscal tools. But a quantity shock tests buffer stocks and the reach of delivery systems and therefore the capacity of the state itself,â she added.





Sitharaman said supply chains optimised for cost alone carry hidden fragility. To replace fragile single-source dependencies with domestic operational depth, the government has launched programmes focused on critical minerals and rare earths, semiconductors and small modular nuclear reactors.

She said for India, resilience means building upon the structural foundations laid over the past decade such as entrepreneurial growth, focusing on efficient last-mile delivery, infrastructure creation and managing prices, essential supplies and external pressures.

âThe test of the coming years will again be partly invisible: the shocks India absorbs without disruption to households and enterprises.â

The evidence of resilience lies in the counterfactual, in the outcomes that did not materialise, such as an inflation spiral that did not take hold, queues that did not form at the fuel outlets, banking stress that did not surface and a fiscal correction that was never forced. âThese counterfactuals deserve as much attention from economists as the headline growth rate,â she added.

World.title: Hormuz blocked, but Gulf crude shipments at pre-war level
World.content:
Disruptions to energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz notwithstanding, crude shipments from the West Asian Gulf region, excluding Iran, have returned to pre-war levels as countries cut dependence on oil tankers to navigate through the choked strait.

According to maritime intelligence and research firm Kpler, at least 16.5 million barrels per day (mbd) of crude left the region between Sept 1 and 28, matching the prewar average. During the peak of the West Asia war in March, the average was 10.5 mbd.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

While 83% of the regionâs crude crossed Hormuz before the war, 40% was exported in Sept through pipelines in Saudi Arabia and the UAE without crossing the key chokepoint.

Of the remaining 60% that physically crossed Hormuz, most was moved using shuttle tankers, Emmanuel Belostrino, head of global crude and geopolitical market data at Kpler, said in his analysis.

Belostrino said more than 70% of the crude that crossed the Strait of Hormuz in Aug changed tankers offshore in the Gulf of Oman.

Crude via other routes made up the difference

Confirmed crude crossings were still more than a quarter below the pre-war level, but volumes moving through alternative routes had more than doubled and made up almost exactly the difference. Saudi pushed more crude through the east-west pipeline to Yanbu, with loadings rising from 0.8 mbd before the war to 4.3 mbd in June. UAE sent crude through the Abu Dhabi crude oil pipeline to Fujairah, where loadings rose from 1.1 mbd to 2.7 mbd.

325 million barrels released from oil reserves: IEA

The International Energy Agency said member countries had released 325 million barrels of oil and oil products from strategic reserves, out of 400 million barrels pledged in March.

World.title: Indians live longer than Pakistanis, lag Bangladeshis, says WHO
World.content:
The logic behind the measure is that hospitals may order additional diagnostic tests, recommend procedures and extend hospital stays when patients have comprehensive insurance cover.

In 2 years from 2021, India regained 2.9 years of expected lifespan: WHO

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indians can expect to live longer than their counterparts in Pakistan, but have shorter lives than people in Bangladesh, the US and Canada, according to the latest World Health Organization estimates.India's life expectancy at birth was 71 years in 2023, compared with 68.2 years in Pakistan, 72.7 years in Bangladesh, 78.5 years in the US and 81.4 years in Canada. But living longer does not necessarily mean living more years in good health. India's healthy life expectancy was 60.6 years in 2023, compared with 60.5 in 2019. It had fallen to 58.4 years in 2021 before recovering to 60.2 years in 2022. The figures are part of WHO's Global Health Estimates, released Friday, covering life expectancy, healthy life expectancy, causes of death and disease burden from 2000 to 2023. WHO said global life expectancy recovered close to pre-pandemic levels, while healthy life expectancy has recovered more slowly.For India, the difference is particularly visible over the pandemic years. Life expectancy fell from 70.5 years in 2019 to 68.1 years in 2021 before rising to 70.5 years in 2022 and 71 years in 2023. In just two years, India regained 2.9 years of expected lifespan.Healthy life expectancy, however, recovered by only 2.2 years, from 58.4 years in 2021 to 60.6 years in 2023, leaving it just 0.1 year above the 2019 level.The gap is also visible among older Indians. At age 60, a person could expect another 18.8 years of life in 2023, compared with 18.4 years in 2019. But 13.7 of those years were expected to be lived in full health, up from 13.4 years in 2019.Indiaâs disease profile has changed sharply. Communicable diseases, such as tuberculosis and diarrhoeal infections, can spread from person to person, while non-communicable diseases (NCDs), such as heart disease, stroke and diabetes, are generally long-term conditions.In 2000, communicable diseases accounted for nearly 62% of the combined death rate from the countryâs 10 leading causes, while NCDs accounted for 34%. By 2023, the pattern had reversed, with NCDs accounting for nearly 75% and communicable diseases 16% of the combined death rate from the top 10 causes. The rest was from injuries.The shift is evident in the leading causes. In 2000, tuberculosis and diarrhoeal diseases topped the list, with 92.4 and 87.8 deaths per 100,000 population. By 2023, ischaemic heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, stroke and diabetes were among the leading causes, with rates of 138.5, 83.19, 74.8 and 49.01, respectively. Yet infectious diseases remain a significant burden, with diarrhoeal diseases, tuberculosis and lower respiratory infections still among Indiaâs top 10 causes of death in 2023.Globally, the shift towards chronic diseases is also pronounced. NCDs accounted for 74% of deaths in 2023, up from 58% in 2000, while eight of the worldâs 10 leading causes of death were NCDs. Global life expectancy reached 73.3 years in 2023, almost back to the 73.4 years recorded in 2019, while healthy life expectancy stood at 62.8 years, still 0.4 years below its 2019 level.

World.title: Watch: Netanyahu invites PM Modi, pilot Smit Machchhar to Israel I-Day event
World.content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin

has invited Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar to light a flame at Israel's Independence Day event, calling him a "hero" of Israel, India and the entire world for foiling an alleged attempt to crash an Israel-bound flydubai flight.

Netanyahu spoke to the 38-year-old pilot on Saturday while Machchhar was undergoing treatment at a hospital in the UAE. During the emotional conversation, Machchhar recounted how he was attacked by his co-pilot inside the cockpit and revealed new details about the incident.

"It's our highest honour that we give on our Independence Day. It's usually reserved for Israeli citizens, but I think here in this case, all the citizens of Israel will embrace you.

They do now, and they will then too. So we hope to see you very soon in Israel," Netanyahu told Machchhar.

The Israeli Prime Minister's office later said on X, "You are a hero for Israel, India, and the entire world. I invite Prime Minister Narendra Modi and you to light a flame on Israeli Independence Day."

"During the emotional conversation that took place this evening, the Prime Minister asked Captain Machchhar how it all started, and Machchhar revealed new details about the terrifying moments in the cockpit," the post said.





Machchhar told Netanyahu that the co-pilot had wanted to pray before the attack. He said he looked towards the front of the cockpit out of respect while the co-pilot prayed.

"...while he was praying, out of respect, I was just looking at the front and not at the back, and suddenly, after, I would say about four-five minutes, there was a big blow to the back of my head.

"My first thought was that there was catastrophic damage to the aircraft and something was not right.

But then after that, the blows kept coming one after the other, and that's when I realised that it's not the aircraft, it's the other guy who was in the cockpit with me," Machchhar said.

Netanyahu praised the pilot for his actions during the incident.

"You saved so many souls. I think you saved something bigger. You saved the spirit of the world...It's something that is being justly hailed around the world. You're a hero of Israel.

You're a hero of India. You're a hero of the entire world," Netanyahu told Machchhar.

"You know, I guess it's a twist of fate, and a twist of faith, and what you did is remarkable. I heard, of course, from the Israeli passengers what transpired after that, and you're a great hero, and you were accompanied by heroes, and you saved the day," he said.

Netanyahu also told Machchhar he was "amazed at his courage" and "at your coolness of judgment under impossible conditions."

The incident took place on Wednesday aboard flydubai flight FZ1073, which was carrying 174 passengers to Israel. Machchhar was allegedly attacked by his co-pilot with a crash axe, an emergency tool kept inside the cockpit.

The aircraft transmitted emergency signals and made a rapid descent of more than 17,000 feet, from 34,000 feet. It eventually made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. The descent was so extreme that part of the aircraft's rudder was reportedly torn away.

The co-pilot has been identified as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami, according to a Wall Street Journal report citing people familiar with the matter.

Machchhar received initial treatment in Tabuk before being shifted to Abu Dhabi for continued medical care.

World.title: NHRC seeks probe into alleged use of minors at CJP’s Mumbai protest
World.content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) on Saturday (October 3, 2026) took cognisance of allegations that minors were involved in a Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest in Mumbai on Friday (October 2, 2026) and that their images were circulated online.

Based on complaints from Sewa Nyaya Utthan Foundation and another organisation, the commission directed the Mumbai Police to investigate the matter and submit an Action Taken Report (ATR) within one week.

The organisations cited posts on X allegedly showing a young child being held above a crowd carrying the National Flag and a placard, while slogans were raised and people recorded the child.

The complaints alleged that persons associated with the Cockroach Janta Party had involved minors in the protest and called for the roles of the organisers, accompanying adults and others who facilitated their participation to be examined.

The complaints also cited purported group chats in which the participation of minors in the protest was allegedly planned, with some participants suggesting that their status as minors could prevent the police from detaining them. The commission said the material indicated that some persons described as minors were also part of these discussions and had allegedly agreed to participate.

Thousands turn up for CJP protest in Mumbai seeking CEC’s resignation; CPI(M) condemns detention of youngsters in Delhi | ECI protest updates

Stating that the allegations raised concerns over the dignity, safety, privacy and possible exploitation of children, a Bench headed by NHRC member Priyank Kanoongo directed the Mumbai Police to examine how the children came to be involved in the October 2 gathering and investigate the roles of organisers, coordinators, accompanying adults and others who may have facilitated their participation. The police have also been asked to examine the other allegations made in the complaints.

The NHRC names Ajinkya Shinde, Abhijit Dipke and Saurav Das among those whose roles and communications are to be examined, while making clear that responsibility must be determined based on evidence.

The commission has also directed X Corp. to preserve the digital trail linked to the content, including account details, URLs, post IDs, timestamps and metadata, and provide information on any moderation or enforcement action taken.

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has been asked to examine X Corp.’s compliance with legal and regulatory obligations relating to child safety, preservation of information and assistance to law enforcement agencies.

The NHRC has also directed the Principal Secretary, Maharashtra Women and Child Development Department, to ensure rescue, care and protection of children as per the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.

Mumbai Police registers FIR against protest organisers

Meanwhile, an FIR was registered at the Shivaji Park police station under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Maharashtra Police Act, based on a complaint, made by Shivaji Park resident Siddhi Deolekar, which named CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke among others. According to the FIR, 400-500 protesters gathered near Gate No. 6 of the Shivaji Park grounds in Dadar West around 2 p.m. and remained there until 7 p.m.

Police said the gathering took place on a road, disrupted traffic, and created a law-and-order situation. Loudspeakers were used without permission.

(With inputs from Chinmay Gaikwad)

World.title: North Korea says it conducted intermediate-range strategic missile drill
World.content:
North Korea fired an intermediate-range missile in a ⁠test overseen by leader Kim Jong Un, state media KCNA reported on Sunday (October 4, 2026).

KCNA said the missile was launched on Saturday (October 3, 2026) from eastern North Korea ‌and hit a target 1,000 km (621 miles) in the sea off the country’s east coast. It said ‌the drill was intended to train troops operating a hypersonic ‌strategic ⁠weapon system and to assess the reliability, efficiency and ⁠mobility of the country’s war deterrent.

The launch was the latest in a series of North Korean weapons tests this year and came as tensions on the ​Korean peninsula escalated over a ‌landmine blast in the Demilitarized Zone last month that wounded South Korean soldiers.

The KCNA report provided additional details about the missile launch disclosed on Saturday by Kim Yo Jong, the sister of Kim ‌Jong Un and a senior official in the ​ruling Workers’ Party.

Kim Yo Jong said South Korea and Japan had failed to track the weapon’s flight, saying ⁠a special “wave-like trajectory mode” had exposed limitations in their tracking capabilities.

South Korea’s military said on Saturday (October 3, 2026) it had detected a ballistic missile ‌launch by North Korea and assessed the missile had flown more than 700 km toward the sea off its eastern coast.

According to KCNA on Sunday (October 4, 2026), Kim Jong Un said Pyongyang must continue efforts to make its enemies recognise the “reliability and fatality” of its strategic offensive weapons and reaffirmed that developing its nuclear ‌war deterrent remained essential for national security.

The test came amid heightened tensions ​after Kim Yo Jong issued a sharply worded statement on Friday (October 2, 2026) rejecting Seoul’s demand for an apology over the ⁠landmine blast in the Demilitarized Zone that seriously wounded South Korean ⁠soldiers.

South Korea has blamed North Korea for planting the mines and called for an apology. Kim Yo Jong ‌called Seoul’s accusation “groundless” and said North Korea had not deliberately laid mines targeting South Korean troops.

North Korea has carried out ​more than 10 missile tests this year.

World.title: Yemen’s Houthis say they attacked Aramco facility in Riyadh with missiles, drones
World.content:
Yemen’s ​Iran-aligned Houthis said on Saturday (October 3, 2026) they ‌had targeted an Aramco ​facility in the ⁠Saudi capital Riyadh with ballistic missiles and drones, saying the attack was in ‌retaliation for Saudi attacks on Yemen’s Sanaa ‌and other provinces.

A large plume ‌of ⁠smoke and fire was ⁠seen rising in the vicinity of an Aramco facility in Riyadh earlier ​on Saturday (October 3, 2026), ‌a witness told Reuters.

There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi authorities of an attack on an ‌Aramco facility. Aramco did ​not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The ⁠reported attack comes amid escalating hostilities between Saudi Arabia and ‌the Houthis, who have stepped up attacks on Saudi cities and energy infrastructure.

The Houthis said last week they had attacked Saudi Aramco facilities ‌in Yanbu with missiles and drones. ​Saudi Arabia said at the time that it had ⁠intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by ⁠the Houthis towards Taif and the Yanbu area, ‌but did not report damage to Aramco facilities.

World.title: Lokesh outlines State’s strategy to become leading destination
World.content:
Andhra Pradesh is working to transform itself into a developed State and contribute to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of a Viksit Bharat, says HRD Minister Nara Lokesh.

Speaking at the Pan-IIT Summit 2026 here on Saturday, Mr. Lokesh said the State government’s strategy was centred on “speed, service and stability,” with a focus on converting investment commitments into projects, jobs and long-term economic growth.

He said the government was targeting leadership across key sectors and relying on a combination of experienced leadership and a younger political team. “Nearly half of the MLAs and 17 of the 25 Ministers are first-time legislators and Ministers respectively,” he said.

On governance, Mr. Lokesh said policies should withstand legal scrutiny and political transitions. He said the government was using Artificial Intelligence to analyse previous recruitment orders and court cases while framing new policies. He cited the recruitment of nearly 16,000 teachers as an example of using technology to identify weaknesses in earlier processes and reduce the risk of legal challenges.

The Minister said the State was moving beyond signing MoUs to ensuring their implementation. He cited the proposed Indian School of Agriculture at Madanapalle, which was intended to support an integrated horticulture ecosystem covering research, mechanisation, processing and market access. “The government estimates the ecosystem can attract investments of nearly ₹1 lakh crore,” he said.

Mr. Lokesh also referred to the proposed 17-million-tonne ArcelorMittal greenfield steel project, saying that it progressed from initial discussions with Aditya Mittal to foundation-laying in about 17 months, including environmental clearances.

He said the Google data-centre investment had strengthened Visakhapatnam’s position on the global technology map and credited coordination between the State and Union governments for resolving regulatory and taxation issues.

Growth clusters

He said Andhra Pradesh was also supporting emerging sectors such as space, drones and quantum technology. The government had allotted 300 acres to space startup Skyroot, while waterfront access had been provided to maritime-drone company Sagar Defence.

The State was developing 23 sectoral growth clusters covering areas including horticulture, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, automotive, renewable energy, solar manufacturing, semiconductors, quantum technology, space and defence, he said, adding that Andhra Pradesh added about 4.8 GW of renewable-energy capacity in a year and aimed to move from third position to first.

He stressed the need for both vertical integration of industrial supply chains and horizontal integration linking industry with education, skills, research and testing, and urged the Pan-IIT community to help connect Andhra Pradesh with industry experts and alumni to strengthen the State’s cluster strategy. He also called for collaboration on what he termed “Visible Governance, Invisible Government” by institutionalising faster government processes.

On Amaravati, Mr. Lokesh said the government was developing the capital as a major urban, education and research hub. He also announced plans for a 5,000-acre greenfield airport in Amaravati.

World.title: Kharge writes to PM and HM
World.content:
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah seeking their intervention in providing help for drought-affected Karnataka.

In his letter, Mr. Kharge said that Karnataka is staring at what could perhaps be the worst drought in 150 years and facing such a drought is impossible without adequate help from the Centre. He made specific requests, including focus on the State’s small and marginal farmers and the dry Hyderabad-Karnataka belt.

Mr. Kharge asked Mr. Modi and Mr. Shah to calculate input subsidy based on Karnataka’s updated Bhoomi land records rather than the outdated 2015-16 Agriculture Census, so that no genuinely eligible farmer is excluded. “Provide enhanced support for drinking water security and the cost of substitute power, particularly in view of historically low reservoir levels in the Cauvery and hydel catchments,” he further said.

World.title: Sagardighi MLA Bayron Biswas sustains burn injuries after fire erupts at West Bengal residence
World.content:
Murshidabad district’s Sagardighi constituency MLA Bayron Biswas suffered burn injuries after a fire broke out at his home in Samserganj on Saturday (October 3, 2026).

He was initially admitted to a local nursing home, and may be transferred to the Murshidabad Medical College and Hospital for better treatment. The family members have also said that he may be transferred to a hospital in Kolkata if the need arises.

According to local sources, Mr Biswas is currently in a stable condition and is undergoing treatment and has sustained around 30% burns. Reportedly. His wife also sustained injuries in the fire while she was attempting to rescue him.

Firefighters rushed to the spot and attempted to douse the fire. However, the cause of the fire has not yet been determined by the officials. The fire had broken out at around 11 a.m., according to the locals present in the area.

Bishnupada Roy, Officer-in-Charge of the Dhuliyan Fire Station, stated on Saturday (October 3, 2026) afternoon, “Three fire tenders brought the blaze under control within an hour. The cause of the fire is not yet clear.”

Mr Biswas is one of the MLAs in the Democratic Trinamool Congress who defected from the Mamata Banerjee faction after the 2026 Assembly elections and set up their own camp under Ritabrata Banerjee’s leadership. He had won from the Sagardighi seat on a Congress ticket in a 2023 bypoll, but later shifted to Mamata Banerjee’s Trinamool.

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari wished him a speedy recovery. “I have heard about it and will get details of the matter,” Mr Adhikari told reporters.

“Deeply disturbed & pained with the news of my friend and colleague Bayron Biswas. Wishing for his speedy recovery. Get well soon Brother,” Mr. Ritabrata Banerjee reacted to the accident and wrote on social media.

Senior Congress leader Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury said that Mr Biswas was like his brother, even if they are in different political parties, and wished for his speedy recovery.

“This needs to be investigated because the fire occurred against the backdrop of his colourful political career,” West Bengal Congress president Subhankar Sarkar said.

World.title: Panchayat elections in Rajasthan to be held in four phases from October 23
World.content:
Elections to the Panchayati Raj institutions in Rajasthan will be held in four phases, from October 23 to November 17, and the results for Zila Parishads and Panchayat Samitis will be announced on November 20. The State Election Commission released the poll schedule in Jaipur on Saturday (October 3, 2026), while stating that 4.03 crore voters would be eligible to exercise their franchise.

State Election Commissioner Rajeshwar Singh said at a press conference that the elections would be held for members of 41 Zila Parishads, 457 Panchayat Samitis and 14,403 village panchayats following delimitation and reorganisation of Panchayati Raj institutions.

Polling for Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti members will be held in four phases on October 23, October 29, November 4 and November 14. Elections for the posts of panch and sarpanch will be held on October 25, October 31, November 6 and November 16.

Mr. Singh said the counting of votes for panch and sarpanch would be taken up immediately after polling at the respective village panchayat headquarters. Elections for deputy sarpanch will be held on October 26, November 1, November 7 and November 17 for the respective phases.

As many as 45,384 polling stations will be set up across the State, while the model code of conduct came into force in the rural areas following the announcement of the election schedule. There will be 50% reservation for women in the Panchayati Raj institutions.

The number of electors in the villages has increased by 6.22% in comparison with the previous panchayat elections held in 2020-21. The elections for Zila Pramukh will be held on November 25 and Up-Zila Pramukh on November 26. Panchayat Samiti Pradhans will be elected on November 27 and Up-Pradhans on November 28.

Mr. Singh said the elections for the three-tier Panchayati Raj institutions were being held simultaneously, as the State Election Commission was fully committed to implementing the ‘One State, One Election’ concept.

“Elections for sarpanch and panch will be conducted using ballot papers, while electronic voting machines will be used for Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti members,” Mr. Singh said. The reorganisation of Panchayati Raj bodies has led to an increase in the number of Zila Parishads from 33 to 41 and Panchayat Samitis from 352 to 457.

World.title: Odisha Governor directs filling of teaching posts amid 70% vacancy in public universities
World.content:
With 70% teachers’ posts lying vacant in State-run universities across Odisha, Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati, who is also Chancellor of the Universities, on Saturday (October 3, 2026) directed to initiate the recruitment process for vacant teaching posts by the first week of November and complete it by the end of the month.

Speaking at a meeting on the ongoing recruitment of teaching faculty in State public universities at Lok Bhavan premises here, Mr. Kambhampati said, “filling vacant teaching posts was the next major challenge after the appointment of Vice-Chancellors in State universities.”

It is to be mentioned that Vice-Chancellors of 14 Universities were appointed on a single day after he assumed office as Governor.

“Merit should be the priority in the appointment of teaching faculty. Quality and merit cannot be compromised,” Mr. Kambhampati said, stressing the need to recruit the best available faculty.

“All eligible applicants be called for interviews instead of extensive shortlisting and scrutiny at the initial stage. Such a process would ensure that no eligible candidate felt excluded while giving interview panels a wider pool of candidates to choose from,” he said.

The Mohan Charan Majhi Government recently informed Odisha Legislative Assembly that as against 2,081 sanctioned posts, 1,441 positions were lying vacant in 17 public universities across the State. To deal with large-scale vacancies, as many as 825 guest faculties have been engaged.

Utkal University, one of the largest universities in Odisha, has about 57.78% (141) of total 244 sanctioned posts of Professor, Associate Professor and Assistant Professors vacant.

Ravenshaw University, oldest of all universities, has 267 sanctioned posts of which 167 posts were lying vacant. As per the information tabled in State Assembly, Madhusudan Law University, Odisha State Open University and Khalikote Unitary University are also yet to fill up vacant posts permanently. In Dharanidhar University, located in home constituency of Odisha CM, of the 128 sanctioned posts, 106 posts are empty. The university is managing academic activities with help of 68 guest faculties.

Mr. Kambhampati also sought details from universities pursuing accreditation and suggested a common tenure for vice-chancellors across public universities. “There are some universities where the vice-chancellor has a three-year tenure and some have four years. There should be a common tenure,” he said.

World.title: After hours of negotiations, second round of govt-opposition talks ends in a 'deadlock'
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Hours-long negotiations between the government and the opposition during a second round of talks ended in a “deadlock” early on Sunday.

The meeting at Parliament House began after 4pm on Saturday, with discussions focusing on the PTI’s planned Oct 4 march to Islamabad. Details on the negotiating process were sparse as both sides seemingly agreed not to speak to the media before matters concluded.

However, shortly before 3am on Sunday, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, who was part of the opposition delegation, told the media that the talks had not succeeded in a breakthrough.

“Deadlock,” he told reporters waiting at Parliament House in footage aired on Geo News. Asked what the points of contention were, he said they were “small things”. He added that the “issue” of meetings with PTI founder Imran Khan could not be solved.

He went on to say that the deadlock was over Imran’s meeting with his personal physicians, and how to address terrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He said that talks had now ended, adding that a detailed press conference would be held later.

Separately, PPP’s Sherry Rehman, who also participated in the talks, said the government delegation debated all points with the opposition.

“Unfortunately, the draft [agreement] was changed four times after it was agreed upon,” she told Geo News, adding that she would not go into the details.

Speaking to reporters, PTI interim chairman Barrister Gohar Khan said that the party’s long march was “intact” and would go ahead. At the same time, he asserted that imposing an emergency or governor rule was not the answer to the protest.

He further said that the participants had also not reached an agreement on when the next round of talks would take place.

He said that the opposition’s demands presented during the second round of talks were “simple” and included meetings with Imran and his spouse, Bushra Bibi.

He said that there were a few issues pertaining to terrorism, where the negotiating process became “stuck”.

Hours-long talks

Visuals broadcast by DawnNewsTV after 9:30pm showed Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi — part of the government delegation — departing Parliament House with a document in his hand, with media reports suggesting he was likely to consult the president.

More than an hour later, footage showed Naqvi returning to Parliament House, with the interior minister maintaining his silence as reporters swarmed him for queries.

The meeting, chaired by National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq, was aimed at defusing the country’s ongoing political crisis. The PTI’s planned Oct 4 protest march, aimed at demanding Imran’s release, has emerged as the latest point of contention between the party and the federal government.

Even as extended talks kept hopes for an agreement alive, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi remained adamant on proceeding with PTI’s march to Islamabad.

After voicing his determination on Saturday afternoon — which irked government representatives — the KP CM again took to X at 12:46am to detail the itinerary for the protest march.

Laying out the journey plan, Afridi said PTI supporters from the districts of Tank, Dera Ismail Khan, South Waziristan, North Waziristan, Bannu, and Lakki Marwat will join the long march from Lakki Marwat’s Gandi Chowk Lakki Marwat at 1pm on Oct 4.

The caravan will halt for the night near Karak, from where people will depart at 12:30pm the next day and stay overnight near Kohat.

Then, at 12pm on Oct 6, protesters from Kohat, Hangu, Kurram, and Orakzai will join the convoy, which will move towards Peshawar and spend the night near Mattani.

The KP CM’s post went on to say that the caravan will depart from Budh Bair in Peshawar on Oct 7 afternoon. “The remaining constituencies of Peshawar will join us at Kohat Road Bridge and the Motorway Toll Plaza. And we will spend the night near Charsadda Interchange.”

They would then depart the Charsadda Interchange at 12:30pm on Oct 8 after people from Charsadda and Mohmand join them.

Refraining from detailing the final leg of the trip to the federal capital, Afridi said the people “of entire KP” would gather at Khairabad on Oct 8 and spend the night there. “God willing, the plan for the next phase will be announced there.”

NA speaker hopes for ‘cordial’ talks

When the huddle began, the NA speaker expressed his hope that the talks would proceed in the same “cordial atmosphere” as Friday’s, according to a post on the NA’s X account.
